## One. Report to Shareholders

## I. 2022 business results

## 1. Achievements of the business plan

Looking back at the past year in Taiwan, the economies of various industries have still been affected by the global economic slowdown and the COVID-19 pandemic. However, as the post-pandemic era approaches, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. has continued to seize new  business  opportunities  after  the  crisis,  actively  laying  out  its  future  plans,  and expanding their presence by opening a total of 16 new stores in 2022, most of which are community-type stores, and expanding into four hospital-type shopping malls. As of 2022, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. has accumulated 319 stores and 26 shopping malls in Taiwan and Mainland China. In 2022, for the first time, the Company also entered the public tertiary (best) hospitals shopping malls in Mainland China through public tender process achieving an important milestone in the layout of its business in both sides of the Taiwan  Strait.  The  Company's  annual  consolidated  revenue  reached  a  historic  high  of NT$7.22 billion, with a net profit after tax of NT$176 million, and a stable gross profit margin of 30%.

The global COVID-19 pandemic has swept globally for over three years, and people have gradually learned to coexist with the virus. The COVID-19 pandemic has brought about significant changes in consumer behavior and has increased public awareness of preventive healthcare. In order to seize potential new business opportunities in the COVID-19 postpandemic era, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. will continue to optimize its first core medical  device  products  through  cooperation  with  suppliers  in  2022.  We  will  offer exclusive agency for custom-made products, as well as expanding our second core business with proprietary health supplements.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. has been aggressively expanding  its  market  share  by  continuously  opening  new  stores  and  attracting  new customers.  In  addition  to  expanding  its  physical  channels,  we  have  also  been  actively innovating its digital online services. In late 2021, it launched the "Online Purchase APP", pioneering the OMO retail model for medical retailing both online and offline. In 2022, we integrated  online  and  offline  consumption  models,  leading  our  physical  and  digital members to cross-refer each other, and achieve precise marketing through big data analysis. Official LINE@ accont of Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc., 'Medfirst Happy Life', had over 1.4 million members by the end of 2022, with a binding rate of nearly 90%. In the future. Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. will continue to consolidate its member base, aiming  at  member  business  opportunities,  and  having  a  solid  foundation  for  corporate development.

Furthermore, in 2022, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. introduced a new service model

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- subscription-based services - an innovative digital service that allows customers to choose their  own  delivery  frequency  and  to  develop  regular  purchasing  habits.  This  model increases customer retention and integrates online and offline platforms, customers can place orders online and have them regularly delivered to their homes through Medfirst intelligent  logistics  center,  strengthening  member  satisfaction  and  cultivating  loyal members.

The global ESG trend continues to gain momentum, and while Anny is striving to drive revenue growth, it is also actively involved in ESG. It regularly hosts the "Thousand Miles of Care " event for public welfare, which combines health education, health checks, and fun  activities  to  promote  the  concepts  of  "seniors  caring  for  seniors"  and  "self-care," increase public health knowledge and caregiving skills, and improve quality of life. By the end of 2022, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. has held over 350 "Thousand Miles of Care " events throughout Taiwan, reaching thousands of community residents. The Company also  promotes  health  and  caregiving  knowledge  through  its  official  website  and  social media platforms, reaching even more people and promoting preventative care. In terms of environmental sustainability, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. new stores and shopping malls  mostly  use  environmentally  friendly  building  materials,  while  the  Company internally optimizes digital systems to reduce paper usage and protect the environment. On the path to sustainable operation, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. continues to strengthen employee education and training, not only to enhance company competitive capabilities, but also to increase product variety, and improve service quality through digital information optimization. In 2022, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. awarded the APEA Asia-Pacific Outstanding  Enterprise  Award  -  Excellence  and  Inspiration  Brand  Award,  earning international recognition as a benchmark enterprise in the medical supplies retail industry. In  the  future,  Medfirst  Healthcare  Services,  Inc.  will  continue  to  uphold  its  corporate mission  of  becoming  "your  family's  health  management  consultant"  and  strive  to improving people's quality of life.

## 2. Budget implementation

We do not provide financial forecasts for 2022 and hence do not need to disclose the budget implementation status.

## 3. Financials

In 2022, the net cash inflows from operating activities totaled NT$1,069,080 thousand, net cash  outflows  from  investing  activities  NT$221,488  thousand,  net  cash  outflows  from financing activities NT$611,301 thousand. In sum, the net cash inflows were NT$245,778 thousand for 2022. Going forward, the opening of new stores is expected to boost revenues significantly.

## 5. R&amp;D status

The  Company  and  its  subsidiaries  are  a  chain  of  retailers  for  professional  medicare products. There is no R&amp;D department and hence no R&amp;D expenses. However, we will carefully consider whether R&amp;D can create synergies and protect shareholders' interest in case of needs to engage in R&amp;D activities for business development.

## II. 2023 business plan outline

1. Business highlights
- (1) Continues  to  expand  footprint  in  Taiwan  and  China  by  accelerating  channel development and pushing the growth momentum.
- (2) Utilizes smart logistics for a wide range of products to complete the supply chain and

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

continues to maximize the development momentum.

- (3) Constructs a comprehensive digital platform for digital transformation on all fronts. Integration of online and offline services to create a new retail and service model and drive the sustainability development of the company.
- (4) Promotes own brands,  provide  more  complete  products  and  services,  expand  the footprint of new businesses and strive for sustainable development of the company.
- (5) Introducing  a  platinum  membership  system  that  provides  prestigious  services. Consolidating loyal members and actively attracting new customers in parallel will bring growth momentum to the company.

## 2. Expected sales and basis for assumptions

In recent years, with the advent of an aging society and the COVID-19 post-pandemic era, the public's awareness of healthcare and preventive care has been raised, leading to an increase in market demand. The statistics from the Ministry of Economic Affairs suggest that  the  retail  sales  of  pharmaceuticals,  medicare  products  and  cosmetics  have  been expanding  over  the  years.  In  2022,  the  total  sales  reached  NT$214.6  billion.  Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. will continue to develop service premises and enlarge market shares  with  digital  transformation  and  by  leveraging  the  Smart  Logistics  Center.  The enhancement of logistic effectiveness will support continued growth in sales.

## 3. Key policies in production and marketing

We are a chain store and distributor of medicare products and not involved in production or manufacturing. Our focus is on distribution, product sale, development and agency and consultation in healthcare. The primary categories are medicare, healthcare and biotech health  products. To  achieve  our  mission  as  the health  manager  of  your  family,  we  will continue to introduce health related products, provide a friendly and convenient shopping environment and services and strive to enhance the quality of life for the public.

## III. Development strategy

In 2023, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. will continue to strengthen its services and product structures across all channels, optimize its store display strategy, innovate and improve digital services,  and  enhance  the  quality  of  professional  services.  The  goals  are  to  extend  from hospitals to communities and neighborhoods, with hospital services as the core, and to extend the industry chain based on customer needs to promote product upgrades and integrate highquality online and offline services, aiming to establish long-term and stable connections with customers, and continue to improve the quality of medical channel services in Taiwan.

- IV. Influence  of  the  external  competitive  environment,  legal  environment  and  the  overall operational environment

In recent years, the world has still been affected by the pandemic of Covid-19 variants. In the first half of 2022, Taiwan experienced a surge in demand for epidemic prevention products. Yet in the second half of the year, the government relaxed pandemic -related regulations, and major medical institutions as well as hospitals gradually lifted their patient visitation control measures.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

As a result, patient flow in hospitals gradually increased. On the other hand, the ongoing conflict between  Russia  and  Ukraine  as  well  as  inflation,  have  impacted  the  investment  on  private sector. The Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Executive Yan, estimates that Taiwan's economic growth rate is 2.43% in 2022.

Due to the impact of the pandemic on consumer habits, the awareness of preventive healthcare among  people  in  Taiwan  has  increased. As  the  COVID-19  post-pandemic  era  approaches, Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. will continue to optimize and upgrade its products, providing more  diversified  high-quality  goods,  meanwhile  also  innovating  and  optimizing  digital services.  In  the  future,  Medfirst  Healthcare  Services,  Inc.  will  also  continue  to  expand  its physical stores, actively developing community-based stores in addition to the typical hospitals that  will  allow  Medfirst  Healthcare  Services,  Inc.  professional  services  and  care  to  extend beyond hospitals and into communities. The Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics,  Executive  Yuan,  estimates  a  2.58%  economic  growth  rate  in  2023.  Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc. expects that, by actively pursuing new business opportunities and the benefits of new stores can gradually make contribution, will become one of the driving forces of sustained growth in the post-pandemic era.

Finally, we thank all the shareholders for advice and attention and we hope you can continue to give us your greatest support and encouragement.

We wish all of our shareholders Good health for great life.

Medfirst Healthcare Services, Inc.

Chairman Chen Li-Ju President Tsai Te-Chung

## 5.    Diversity and independence of the board of directors:

## (1) Diversity of the board of directors:

## A. Diversity Policy:

The  Company  advocates  and  respects  the  policy  of  diversity  of  directors  in  order  to strengthen corporate governance and promote the sound development of the composition and  structure  of  the  board  of  directors,  believing  that  the  diversity  approach  will  help enhance the overall performance of the Company. Board members are selected on the basis of merit and have diverse and complementary abilities across industry sectors, including basic composition (e.g., age, gender, nationality, etc.), industry experience and relevant skills  (e.g.,  law,  accounting,  industry,  finance,  marketing,  or  technology),  as  well  as operational judgment, business management, leadership, and crisis management.

## B. Specific Goals:

In order to strengthen the functions of the Board of Directors and achieve the desired goals of corporate governance, Article 20 of the Company's "Corporate Governance Best Practice Principles"  states  that  the  Board  of  Directors  as  a  whole  should  possess  the  following competencies:

- a Operational judgment capabilities
- b. Accounting and financial analysis capabilities
- c. Operational management capabilities
- d. Capabilities to deal with a crisis
- e. Industry-related knowledge
- f. Vision into international markets
- g. Leadership decision
- h.      Decision-making capacity

## C. Achievement

There  are  7  directors  in  the  board  of  directors,  including  4  independent  directors.  The specific management goals and achievements of the Board of Directors' diversity policy are listed below. All the diversity goals have been achieved.

## (III)   Succession planning for the board of directors and key management personnel

## 1.    Succession planning for board members

The Company currently has seven directors (including four independent directors), each with  expertise  in  operation  management,  industry  knowledge,  leadership  and  decisionmaking,  electronic  information,  financial  accounting  and  legal  knowledge.  The  future composition of the board of directors of the company and the background of members will be planned according to the development of the Company.

With respect to the succession planning of the Board of Directors, the Company currently has a number of internal managers with management and professional abilities who can be qualified for the succession of directors, and the Company also seeks external professionals

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

to prepare for the succession planning of directors. As for the independent directors, they are required by laws to have working experience in business, law, finance, accounting or corporate business. The Company will appoint independent directors in accordance with the laws to strengthen corporate governance.

## 2.    Succession planning for key management personnel

For Medfirst's requirements of middle and high-level managers, in addition to professional abilities and practical experience in different fields, we also require that our core values in the management and execution of business are based on our four management philosophies, which  include:  serving  our  customers,  operating  in  a  sustainable  and  decent  manner, providing a full range of professional home health consulting services, and meeting the needs of our employees for self-fulfillment in life and work. From new recruits training to promotion exams, all are based on our corporate culture.

Medfirst Group has a total of more than 40 middle and high-level managers. In addition to regular  monthly  management review meetings  at  the  parent  company  and  subsidiaries, where  the  chairman  and  president  are  personally  instructed,  we  also  set  up  different programs to promote interdepartmental cooperation and business exchanges. In addition to the annual two-day one-night elite training program in the third quarter of each year to gather management personnel from all over Taiwan to enhance management functions, we also  conduct  leadership  training  programs  for  executives  from  time  to  time  to  provide resources to improve their management skills.

In  the  future,  we  plan  to  rotate  our  management  team  to  cultivate  the  multi-faceted professional abilities of middle and high-level managers in order to achieve the goal of nurturing all-around talents, and we expect to select successors of departments from the middle and high-level managers.

<!-- image -->

2. The  policy,  criteria  and  mix  of  compensation  payments,  the  procedures  for  setting compensation, and the relevance to operating performance and future risks:
- (1) In  accordance  with  Article  33  of  the  Company's  Articles  of  Incorporation,  the Company shall set aside 1% to 15% of the annual profit as employee compensation, which shall be distributed in shares or cash by resolution of the Board of Directors. The Company may set aside less than 7% of the above-mentioned profit as director compensation by resolution of the Board of Directors.
- (2) In accordance with the Company's Articles of Incorporation, the directors shall be paid for their attendance at meetings of the Board of Directors. The Chairman's salary, compensation and other benefits of all directors shall be determined by the Board of Directors based on their participation in the Company's operations and the value of their contributions and the prevailing level in the industry.
- (3) The remuneration of our directors and managers is determined in accordance with the Company's Articles of Incorporation and the degree of their contribution to the Company (e.g., their participation in the Company's operations and decisions, their mastery  of  the Company's  objectives  and  tasks,  their contribution to the management of internal relations and communication and internal control, etc.), their duties,  the  Company's  operating  results  for  the  year,  and  the  consideration  of  the Company's future  risks  and  the  reference  to  prevailing  level  in  the  industry. The correlation between their remuneration and operating performance is positive. The amount of remuneration is disclosed in the Annual Report as required by the laws and regulations, and the future risk of the related operations should be limited.
- (4) On August 23, 2012, the Company established the Compensation Committee. The remuneration  of  directors  and  managers  are  discussed  and  resolved  by  the Compensation  Committee  before  being  submitted  to  the  Board  of  Directors  for approval.

3. The duties and responsibilities of Compensation Committee:
- (1) The Committee shall exercise due diligence as a bona fide administrator  to  faithfully fulfill the powers and duties as follows and shall submit the offered proposals to the Board of Directors into discussions:
3. (A) Reassess  on  a  regular  basis  'The  Organizational  Rules  of  the  Compensation Committee' and offer proposal for amendment.
4. (B) Enact and reassess on a regular basis the standards/criteria to evaluate performance of  the  Company's  directors  and  managers,  annual  and  long-term  goals  to  be achieved, remuneration and salary policies, systems as well as the standards and structure, and further disclose into the annual report the contents of the standards/criteria for evaluate performance.
5. (C)    On a regular basis, evaluate the accomplishment of the performance targets by the Company's  directors  and  managers. Further  on  the  grounds  of  assessment outcome and the said standards/criteria, specify their individual salary remuneration with  the  contents  and  amounts.    Expressly  disclose  into  the  annual  report  the results of performance evaluation by the directors and managers, the rationality and interrelationship between the contents and amounts of salaries &amp; remuneration and the results of  performance  evaluation  and  report  all  such  contents  to the

<!-- image -->

shareholders' meeting.

- (2) The  Committee  shall  carry  out  the  responsibilities  and  powers  mentioned  under  the preceding Paragraph according to the principles as follows:
2. (A)    Definitely assure that the Company's arrangements into the salaries &amp; remuneration would live up to laws and ordinances concerned likely to attract top level talents into the Company.
3. (B)    Regarding  the  salaries  &amp;  remuneration  toward  directors  and  managers,  the Company shall take into reference with the normal levels of payments prevalent in firms and companies in the same industry.    The Company shall further take into account the outcome of evaluation of their individual performance, the time spent by them, the duties and responsibilities assumed by them, to accomplish individual targets, the performance in the respective duty positions, the salaries  &amp; remuneration paid by the Company to personnel of the equivalent levels in recent years, the accomplishment of the long-term and short-term targets of the Company, the rationality and relevance of the Company's business performance and potential risks in the future.
4. (C)    Under no circumstances shall the Company try to guide directors and managers into any  behaviors  subject  to  potential  risks  in  an  attempt  to  strive  for  salaries  &amp; remuneration.
5. (D)    Aiming at the ratio of the remuneration payable to directors and senior managers in terms of their short-term performance with partial change of the payment timeframe of the variable salaries &amp; remuneration, the Company shall take into account the characteristics of the business lines and attribute of the Company's business so as to come to final decision as appropriate.
6. (E)    In determination of the contents and amounts of the salaries &amp; remuneration toward directors and managers, the Company should take into account the rationality.    A decision  toward  salaries  &amp;  remuneration  of  directors  and  managers  should  not significantly  deviate  from  the  performance  in  finance.    In  case  of  a  significant profit or prolonged loss, such salaries &amp; remuneration should not be higher than the same  in  the  preceding  year. In  a  case  higher  than  the  preceding  year,  the rationality should be well explained inside the annual report and reported to the shareholders' meeting.
7. (F)    Toward  the  decision  regarding  their  personal  salaries  &amp;  remuneration,  the Committee members shall not participate in the discussion and voting process.
- (3) The term 'salaries &amp; remuneration' as set forth in the two preceding Paragraphs includes cash remuneration, stock options, dividends, retirement benefits or severance benefits, a variety of allowances and other measures with substantial incentives; Such scope should be consistent with the remuneration of directors and managers in the standards for the matters to be recorded in the annual report of a public company.
- (4) Amidst  the  discussion  process  in  response  to  a  proposal  from  the  Compensation Committee, the Board of Directors shall take into over account the amount of salaries &amp; remuneration, the terms of payment and potential risks lying ahead upon the Company in the future.
- (5) Where the Board of Directors rejects or amends a proposal offered by the Compensation Committee, it calls for a decision voted by one half majority of the present directors in

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

the Board meeting which is attended by two-thirds majority of total directors.    During the resolution process, based on the comprehensive  consideration and concrete explanation, the Board of Directors shall concretely explain that whether the salaries &amp; remuneration  finally resolved  would  be  more  superior  to  that  proposed  by  the Compensation Committee.

- (6) In the event that the salaries &amp; remuneration finally resolved by the Board of Directors prove more superior to that proposed by the Compensation Committee, the facts of gaps and  the  reasons  shall  be  expressly  entered  into  the  minutes  of  the  board  of  directors meeting.    The same shall be announced and declared through the information declaration website designated by the competent authority within two (2) days after the decision is resolved in the Board of Directors.
- (7) Where the salaries  &amp;  remuneration  toward  a  subsidiary's  directors  and  managers  are resolved beforehand based on the hierarchical responsibility rule of that subsidiary and should call for approval by the Company's Board of Directors, the present Committee shall come to a proposal before submitting to the Board of Directors into discussion.

(III)  Does the Company assess existing and  potential  risks  and  opportunities  associated  with  climate  change  and  adopt  the  corresponding  responses  and measures?    【  Governance  】  The Chairman and the entire managerial team will assess the potential risks and  opportunities  of  climate  change  and  formulate  strategies  and  objectives  in  response.  1.  Each year, the Board of Directors is presented with data on the electricity  savings and GHG emissions of each department, as well as the actual status  of achieving annual carbon emission reduction targets, in order to help set  new management targets for energy saving/carbon reduction.  2.    In  2019, Medfirst joined hands with logistics and warehousing centers to  introduce clean energy and promote sustainable actions that thread industry's  values. From procurement, contract manufacturing and transportation, to the  delivery  of  products  to  consumers,  each  step  is  integrated  with  considerations for sustainability.  【  Strategies  】  1.  Retail sale stores:  (1)   For signboards of all retail stores, we adopt timing devices to minimize  the energy consumption through the uniquely designed fan function.  (2)   Toward  the  newly  open  stores,  we  elaborately  adopt  environmental  protection and energy-saving label products, e.g., T5 and LED lamps,  inverter air conditioning equipment, air doors and the like to implement  the concept of energy conservation and environmental protection in the  hands-on operation.  (3)   In terms of lighting needs, we adopt LED lighting to meet the entire  needs and also install "smart sensor lighting devices" in certain areas.  The  lighting  function  will  be  activated  when  in  an  event  while  pedestrians pass to primarily prevent unnecessary waste.    We hope that  through such practical actions, we shall let the public understand how  important the energy conservation and carbon reduction.  2.    New logistic warehouses:  (1)   For roofs, we set up with a solar installation system characterized by  pollution-free  when  generating  electricity  from  renewable  energy.  Such a device can help the roof insulation and cooling by up to 3-5  No discrepancy   |

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

<!-- image -->

| degrees  to  save  the  cost  of  air  cooling  and  air  conditioning  to  accomplish the benefits of energy saving and carbon minimization.  (2)   Our  constant  temperature  storage  areas  are  equipped  with  automatic  rolling doors.    The normal temperature area is set on the rooftop and  the  ventilation  equipment  is  set  on  the  walls  where  the  natural  ventilation environment is formed through the convection device with  the positive and negative pressure fan equipment to minimize the power  consumption of the entire air conditioner and the fan systems.  (3)   We widely adopt electric stackers and trailers, giving no chance at all  for use of diesel machinery that tends to pollute the environment.    On  a regular basis, we maintain battery quality to assure adequate charging  efficiency to minimize power loss.  ## 【 Risk management 】  Financial  risks,  due  to  climate  change,  are  addressed  through  annual  targets, budgets and plans set by the President Office, and GHG inventories are conducted in accordance with ISO 14064-1 GHG inventory standards.  ## 【 Indices and targets 】  1.  Reduce  greenhouse  gas  emissions. ## (VI) The Company's share dividend policy and fact of implementation of such policy

## 1. Share dividend policy defined in the Company's Articles of Incorporation

Article 33-1: Where the Company proves to operate into profit in a year, the sums required to pay tax and make up previously accumulated loss, if any, shall be first amortized.    Thereafter, a sum for 10% legal reserve shall be amortized but the legal reserve shall no longer be amortized while the total legal reserve is up to the Company's total paid-in capital.    With the balance, the special reserve shall be duly amortized or rotated.    For the final balance, if any, in combination with the accumulated unappropriated retained earnings, the Board of Directors shall propose percentages  of  distribution  to  be  further  resolved  in  the  shareholders'  meeting  before distribution of dividend bonus is to be distributed to shareholders.

Article  35:  The  Company  holds  a  dividend  policy  in  line  with  the  current  and  future development  plans. With  comprehensive  consideration  of  the  investment  environment, capital  planning  and  domestic  and  foreign  competitive  environments  and  other  factors,  in principle, a sum more than 30% of the surplus available for distribution shall be allocated to shareholders as the bonus.    The bonus may be distributed to shareholders either in cash or in stocks where the cash dividend shall not be less than 10% of aggregate total of all sorts of dividends.

## (VIII)  Compensations to employees, and remuneration to directors and supervisors

1. The  percentage  and  scope  of  remunerations  payable  to  employees,  directors  and supervisors as set forth under the Articles of Incorporation:

Article 33: With the profit earned by the Company, if any, a sum 1% - 15% shall be set aside as remuneration to employees to be attributed either in cash or stock as resolved by the Board of Directors, payable equally to employees of subordinate company (ies) satisfactory to the specified conditions.    With the aforementioned amount of profit, the Company may, as resolved by the Board of Directors, set aside an amount up to 7% maximum  limit  as  the  remuneration  to  directors. The  issues  of  allocations  of remuneration to employees and remuneration to directors shall be duly reported to the shareholders'  meeting. Where  the  Company  remains  in  an  accumulated  loss, nevertheless, the sum to make good the loss shall be withheld beforehand the allocation of  remuneration  to  employees  and  remuneration  to  directors  in  accordance  with  the percentages set forth under the preceding Paragraph.

2. In terms of the grounds to estimate the remunerations payable to employees, directors and supervisors in the current year, the accounting handling manner for the discrepancy between number of shares counted for remuneration to employees through distribution of stocks and the amount of substantial distribution:

Here at the Company in Year 2022, the remuneration to employees and remuneration to directors  were  estimated  at  4%  and  2.2%  of  the  Company's  profit  before  tax  after deduction of remuneration to employees and remuneration to directors.    In case of a discrepancy between the aforementioned estimated amounts and the amounts as actually granted, it shall be duly handled by means of accounting estimation change and entered into account after adjustment in the year of actual payments.

## I. Business

## (I) Scope of business

1. Main business lines

The group is the first  chain  store  selling  medicare  supplies  and  managed  by  a  medical professional  team  in  Taiwan.  We  distribute  medicare,  healthcare  and  biotech/wellness products and provide relevant services. Medfirst Healthcare Services is a leading brand and a chain store of medicare supplies. ## 3. Products and services

The Company primarily sells medicare, healthcare and biotech/wellness products to the public. To achieve our corporate mission as 'the health manager for your family', we will launch  more  health  related  products  and  provide  a  friendly  and  convenient  shopping environment and services to the public.

According to the data, published by the Ministry of Health and Welfare of the Executive Yuan,  the  average  NHE  per  person  in  2021,  was  NT$60,783,  an 8.25% increase from the NT$56,149 reported in 2020. As for the proportion of NHE per capita to GDP per capita, even though the average GDP per capita reached a 10-year high in 2021, the average annual GDP growth rate reached 9.69% and has remained above 6% since 2011, indicating that the expenditures on health care spent by citizens is in generalshowing a steady increase every year.

- B. Change in demographic age profiles in Taiwan and major countries

According to the projections of the population of the Taiwan area, the Republic of China, for 2022-2070 prepared by the National Development Council, the number of seniors aged 65 and above has been rising year over year. In 2017, the size of the old age population surpassed that of the young age population. By 2025, the old age population aged ≥65 is expected to account for over 20% of the entire population, a milestone for the super aged society. This trend will likely generate a large demand for senior care and social insurance payments, which will increase the financial burden on government budgets and the elderly population,  and  so  is  worth  keeping  a  close  watch. The  median  age  of  the population is another indicator: 42.7 in 2020 and 58.2 forecasted for 2070. This will be the second highest in the countries listed below. In sum, the percentage of  the  old  age  population  is  on  a  steady  increase. As  the  society  ages,  the demand for medicare and healthcare, disease monitoring and prevention and hence the expenditures of medical supplies are set to grow.

## (2) Retail market for beauty, health and medical supplies in Taiwan

In the domestic beauty, health and medicare supplies retail market, according to the "Monthly Revenue Statistics" published by the Department of Statistics, MOEA, the market size has grown from $164.8 billion in 2011, to exceed $200 billion in 2022, reaching $214.6 billion. In 2012, the domestic economy and the domestic demand market were affected by the European debt crisis, which slowed down the overall market growth. In recent years, the market has been steadily improving until 2019, when the worldwide outbreak of COVID-19 forced people to avoid going out and changed their spending habits, which dampened the overall growth performance of the beauty, health and medicare supplies retail industry. After the lifting of a number of  restrictions  related  to  the  pandemic  in  2022,  people  resumed  their  normal consumption behaviors, and the entire beauty, health and medicare supplies retail markets collectively generated a growth rate of 8.35% YoY.

Overall, the domestic beauty, health and medical supplies retail market has been on a  growth  trend  this  past  decade,  and  with  the  demographic  changes  and  future demand for long-term care, it is expected to drive the future growth of the medical device industry.

## (3) Medical device market in China

According  to  the  Blue  Book  of  Medical  Device  Industry  in  China  published  by Medical  Institute  of  Shanghai  ZERO-Inventory  (S.Z.I.),  the  Chinese  medicare market shows great potential given the increasing economic development and health demand. The size of the Chinese medical device market grew from RMB 255 billion in  2014  to  RMB  764.8  billion  in  2020. The  large  population  and  the  increase  in income per capita, as well as numerous favorable medicare policies in China are all contributing  to  continued  demand  growth  for  medical  devices.  Policy-wise,  the government of Mainland China is promoting the policies relating to the "12th FiveYear  Plan,  such  as  the  12th  Five-Year  Plan  for  the  Medical  Device  Technology Industry"  and  the  12th  Five-Year  Plan  for  the  Development  of  the  Health  Care Industry, etc. In addition, the recent implementation of the "New Medical Reform" policy is expected to promote consumer health awareness in the post-pandemic era in Mainland China, strengthen consumer awareness and demand for home medical care, and drive the demand for related medical devices to grow continuously.

## (4) Global medical device market

According to a study by BMI Research, the size of the global medical device market was USD 454.3 billion in 2021, up 6.3% from 2020, and is expected to grow to USD 535.2 billion in 2026, with a compound annual growth rate of about 5.6% from 2021 to 2026. In 2021, the global medical device regional market remains dominated by the Americas, Western Europe, and Asia Pacific, together, accounting for 92.9% of the global market. Overall, the top three market rankings are unlikely to change much in the future, but as Asia-Pacific countries gradually move into an aging society, this region will also become the focus of the global medical device industry.

## (5) Biotech and wellness supplements

As the living standards and medical technology advances rapidly around the world, the  quality  of  life  has  been  improving  and  the  average  life  expectancy  is  on  the increase.  This  combined  with  low  birth  rates  means  population  aging  in  both developed and developing countries. The resulting increase in the number of chronic disease patients and seniors poses a heavier burden on national medical expenditures and social benefits. Meanwhile, the advocacy and the implementation of preventive medicine encourages the prevention of diseases with supportive and adjuvant and alternative  therapies.  Due  to  the  enhanced  health  awareness,  preventive  medical supplies are increasingly popular among consumers.

The 2020 pandemic around the world and the increasing treatment of COVID-19 as flu are enhancing the public's awareness in healthcare and virus prevention. Other than mask wearing, frequent handwashing and environmental disinfection, consumers also hope to boost immunity and stay healthy with supplements. This will drive further demand of nutritional supplements and create business opportunities for companies.

According to Euromonitor, the worldwide market size of nutritional supplements reached US$869.7 billion in 2022, with an average Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 5.5%. At the present, North America and Europe are still dominating the market growth, but the changes in growth in Asia Pacific are even more impressive, and it is estimated that its market share will exceed 30% in 2026. With the pandemic, the business opportunities of aging population and the rise of health awareness, the future growth of Taiwan's dietary supplement market is very promising.

## 2. Industry upstream, midstream and downstream

The Company is a chain retailer of medical supplies. At the upstream of the industry chain are the suppliers of a variety of medicare, healthcare and biotech/wellness food ingredients and components. This covers a wide range of plastic and chemical materials, electronic parts,  hardware,  raw  materials  and  ingredients  for  biotech/wellness  foods,  and  other materials.  Sitting  at  the  midstream  are  the  manufacturers  of  medicare  and  healthcare products  and  biotech/wellness  foods.  This  includes  medical  testing  and  monitoring instruments (e.g., electronic blood pressure monitors, thermometers, ear thermometers, air monitoring and temperature control devices), optical medical supplies (e.g., optical lens and contact lens), and  medical consumables (e.g.,  guide tubes  and test  specimens)  and various capsules, caplets and wellness beverages. As a retailer at the downstream of the industry,  the  Company  sells  the  aforesaid  medical  supplies  and  offers  professional consultation to consumers. We are essentially the 'last mile' in the supply chain of medical supplies. Below is a visual representation of the upstream, midstream and downstream of the industry where the Company operates.

## 4. Competition

## (1) Government policies

Six  Emerging  Industries  (i.e.,  medicare,  biotech,  tourism,  green  energy,  quality agriculture  and  creative  culture)  and  Emerging  Smart  Industries  (e.g.,  cloud computing,  smart  electric  cars,  smart  green  buildings  and  industrialization  of inventions and patents) are the priority for the industrial policies of the Executive Yuan.

As far as medicare is concerned, the rising awareness in health and the advancement in medical resources, technology and the environment are all contributing factors. Meanwhile, Taiwan entered the aging society in 1993 and the birth rate has been staying at low level. As the old-age population continued to grow, Taiwan entered the

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

aged society in 2018 and is expected to move towards the super aged society in 2026. By 2065, about four out of every ten people are aged 65 or higher and among the four elderlies, one is over 85 years old. This is the reason why the government's industry policy  seeks  to  address  population  aging,  low  birth  rates,  health  promotion  and disease  management.  The  10-Year  Long-Term  Care  Program  2.0  is  currently underway, with integration  of  social  welfare,  health  and  medicare  resources. The purpose is to establish a community care model and an extensive care network for local aging. Hopefully the wide range of services from family support, homecare, communities to care homes can provide universal access to the care system. With communities serving as the foundation, the system aims to accommodate those in need of long-term care and enhance the quality of life of the cared-for.

To  protect  the  public's  health  and  wellness,  the  Ministry  of  Health  and  Welfare, Executive Yuan in its 2021 agenda covered pertinent issues from welfare services, social security, medicare, long-term care, health promotion, disease prevention and food &amp; drug management, in order to integrate social welfare, health and medicare resources. The  policy and strategic priorities during the year included the establishment of a high-quality long-term care system with comprehensive resources, the broadening of the full-service medicare system to ensure the public's access to medical services and the creation of a top-notch response system against infectious diseases. There are also efforts to encourage R&amp;D in medical science to enhance the medicare industry in Taiwan.

The Medical Devices Act was passed in December 2019 and promulgated on May 1, 2021, to separate the medical device management from the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. There are robust measures over product distribution, transportation quality and safety monitoring of medical devices on the market place. Risks are diversified and categories  for  management,  to  help  the  R&amp;D  and  product  innovation  of  low-risk medical technologies. The new legislation is centered on the lifecycle of medical devices and risk management principles. Certification and accreditation systems are put in place as a mechanism to ensure accountability.

- (2) Growing sophistication in the demand for healthcare

Females  tend  to  be  more  concerned  with  health  and  they  are  mostly  the  main shoppers  for  the  family. As  a  result  of  low  birth  rates,  the  health  of  children  is increasingly  emphasized. The  baby  boomer  generation  who  controls  most  of  the world's economic power is also more aware of preventive medicine compared to the previous generation. The requirements from these consumer segments will drive the demand and business opportunities for healthcare products.

- (3) More focus on prevention than cure for the new generation

The incidence age for many diseases is becoming younger due to unbalanced diet in a busy life. Therefore, consumers are increasingly focused on preventive than cure. The demand for medicare supplies is no longer just for the middle aged and elderlies. Many young adults are increasing medicare expenditures. The stores selling medical supplies are welcoming customers other than the sick or the injured. When it comes to retailers, the key consideration for consumers who spend on preventive medicine are  brands,  reputations,  accessibility  and  after-sales  services. The  new  generation consumers have higher expectations for product and service quality before purchases. Therefore, it is necessary to provide more and better services in order to satisfy the new generation consumers.

<!-- image -->

## (4) Influence of information symmetry on price elasticity

Product information is rather transparent given the intense market competition and ready flows of information. The development of the interactive internet also allows many users to instantly share all kinds of information. This empowers consumers with a better understanding of product attributes and suitability when they purchase medical supplies. The choice of retailers is also part of the information collection process. Hence, prices are not necessarily the sole factor that influences purchase decisions. It is important for retailers to ensure customer relation management and stay on top of consumer behaviors and thinking.

- (5) Digital transformation

The pandemic has created new lifestyles. Digital transformation has become the top priority and operational target for leading companies. It is necessary to respond to the market in a timely manner, to adjust operational guidelines and strategies. New organizational structures and workflows are being developed. Digital technology is redefining  work  styles,  leveraging  suitable  talents,  materials  or  tools  to  satisfy customers'  needs  and  create  needs,  to  capitalize  on  business  opportunities  and effectively establish footprint in the marketplace.

## 5. Technology and R&amp;D

Medfirst is a leading brand among the professional chain stores of medicare supplies. We do not have a dedicated R&amp;D department given our business as a retailer. By gathering the feedback  from  consumers  at  the  front  line,  Product  Marketing  Division  is  proactively developing  products  complementary  to  suppliers'  offerings  via  OEM/ODM  methods. Marketing  strategy  and  channel  promotion  are  planned  accordingly.  In  the  meantime, employee training and education are organized to ensure the rending of comprehensive and professional health consultation to consumers. This is to achieve our brand as the 'health manager of your family'.

## 6. Long-term and short-term business development plans

We aim to deliver Total Solutions, from offline to online, for products and services. The interaction of the selling process delivers values. In addition to the large variety of products for consumers to choose from, our stores provide professional consultation in healthcare. We endeavor to help the public by creating a ubiquitous platform for happiness and health consultations.  This  encompasses  periodical  measurements  to  keep  an  eye  on  potential health problems, information about subsidy applications to assist in home care, visits for medical  devices  maintenance,  health  consultations  to  enhance  the  knowledge  base  of consumers. The emphasis on professional service quality is to meet consumers' needs and to create demand.

## (1) Short-term business development plan

- A. O2O (online-to-offline) and OMO (online-merge-offline)

According to Economic Daily on August 30, 2015, ecommerce was expected to account for 6.5% of sales in the Taiwan retail market in 2020, up from 5.13% in  2014.  This  is  not  a  high  number  after  years  of  vibrant  ecommerce development. The timeliness, services and professionalism of physical stores remain irreplaceable. That said, the development Omni-Channel Retailing is necessary given the growing penetration of the Internet and mobile devices, the change  in  purchase  behavior  and  the  greater  information  distribution  and

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

openness. Medfirst's ecommerce platform serves as another shopping option and allows consumers to collect information online regarding the quality of products.  This  also  highlights  the  importance  of  O2O  (online  to  offline). Consumers can gather product information online but also enjoy the interaction in store. The services with enhanced experience ensure that product quality is recognized by consumers. We also differentiate our services in order to extend the services and professional purpose of medical devices and products. This new retailing service integrates the transaction data of members and safeguards the personal data of consumers, in order to provide services before, during and after sales, to enhance the O2O service quality and strengthen branding and images. Once the penetration of wearables reaches a high level in the future, data access will be even more immediate and convenient. Precision marketing can also be achieved with big data analytics.

As  technology advances, consumers  can  purchase products from ever increasing channels. To ensure the safety of use and to promote the accessibility of medical devices, the Food and Drug Administration, Department of Health, started on November 1, 2012, to allow the distribution of Class I (low risks) medical devices via mail orders. Starting on January 2, 2014, Class II medical devices (such as body fat scales) suitable for home use, non-invasive,  nonimplantable and not requiring professional guidance can be purchased via mail orders. Subsequently the government gradually allowed other Class II medical devices to be sold via mail channel, depending on product characteristics and consumers' demand. The market (and competition) became increasingly open.

Online sale of medical devices integrates and connects with consumers online and offline and resolves the urgent needs for home medicare. Going forward, consumers online will have a wider variety of medicare supplies to choose from. Instance services are also available to consumers in remote regions. Channels play  an  increasingly  comprehensive  role,  from  services  at  the  hospital  to services in the community and even bespoke services at home. The business model is more complete, real-time and highly accessible.

Some  chain  medicare  retailers  are  driving  for  O2O  (online  to  offline),  a business  model  involving  online  shopping  and  offline  experiencing.  Others adopt precision marketing via OMO (online merge offline), to integrate online and offline products with membership services. This is to cater to the needs of members who shop online and offline. For instance, membership information can  be  consolidated  so  that  the  same VIP  benefits  are  available  online  and offline.  The  information  of  online  and  office  transactions  serve  as  an  allinclusive reference for precision marketing and decision-making.

Online services are increasingly comprehensive. Domestic retailers of medicare  supplies  have  broken  the  mold  of  the  old  business  models.  The complete  range  of  products  not  restricted  by  laws  (e.g.,  long-care  assistive devices,  protective  gear,  nutritional  supplements,  incontinence  products  and wellness foods) are available online and delivered to home.

- B. Value delivery

In the past, the word of mouth recommendations were for physical stores where the selection was limited and hence consumers were price oriented. Now that a  large  amount  of  information  travels  far  and  wide  online,  consumers  have

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

become value oriented.  In  other  words,  smart  consumers  purchase  the  best quality  products  at  the  most  reasonable  prices.  They  emphasize  high  costperformance ratios, act upon emotions or pursue customization. It is about trust and  professionalism.  Currently,  the  level  of  consumers'  involvement  is relatively  low  for  the  purchase  of  medical  devices.  Prices  are  not  the  only consideration.  Consumers  require  a  platform  that  offers  professional  health services and a wide range of products. Meanwhile, the creation of the shopping scenario  including  product  displays,  cashiers  and  traffic  flow  arrangements provides a good shopping experience and enables interactive marketing.

## (2) Long-term business development plan

## A. Cloud health management platform

As all levels of hospitals are promoting long-distance care and the public is increasingly  health  conscious,  medical  devices  are  moving  from  cure  to prevention. This involves the establishment of an integrated health management  platform. Algorithms  process  the  information  of  measurement statistics  in  order  to  estimate  and  forecast  requirements  of  consumers. This increases the stickiness of consumers and builds long-term loyalty of customers. Health  management  workflows are  created with  technology,  to  gather  data, compute, estimate and forecast. This empowers the development of business models with innovative services and drives the health-enhancing industry.

Information technology has changed the traditional medicare model. A case in point  is  the  use  of  integrated  information  technologies  for  deployment  of services and long-distance care in the health enhancing industry. For instance, it is possible to establish measurement database and use algorithms to estimate and  forecast  the  requirements  of  diabetes  patients.  This  strengthens  the stickiness of consumers and boosts long-term loyalty of customers. Product displays  are  constantly  evolving  in  order  to  attract  more  consumers  and increase the reach rates.

## B. Customized home care

The rollout of the long-care policy tasks the retails of medical devices with a more  important  responsibility.  In  addition  to  selling  relevant  products  to consumers, there will also be leasing and consultation services. However, it is necessary  to  divide  the  spaces,  retrain  personnel,  replan  the  traffic  flow  of goods and even establish the capabilities in the cleaning and organization of recovered leased items. These are all cost pressure for companies.

Most important, home services will be essential as the size of aged population continues to increase. Product repair and maintenance, space décor and even daily  mean  deliveries  are  all  challenges  to  the  industry's  capability  in integrating  flows  of  goods,  capital  and  information.  Once  assistive  tools become a daily necessity, customized homecare will become mainstream. Onefor-all  products  can  longer  satisfy  picky  customers.  Only  the  professionally trained  sales  team  is  able  to  provide  customized  products  and  services  to consumers.  It  is  necessary  to  establish  a  highly  flexible  system  for  a  large variety of products to manage product specification inquiries and warehouse spaces and to quickly respond to customers' needs. Timely and caring services help  to  understand  the  requirements  of  consumers,  in  order  to  deliver

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

appropriate  medical  knowledge  and  professional  health  advice.  Only  by provide extensive customized products, services and home care can competitive advantages be maintained.

## (2) Market shares

The Company operates a chain store of medicare supplies. According to the 2022 Taiwan Chain Store Yearbook, the number of beauty and health stores in Taiwan totaled 5,946 in 2021. This means we had 4.83% market share measured by our 287 stores at the end of 2021. We continued to grow our footprint by adding 16 stores from 2021 to 2022 and we existed the year 2021 with 303 stores in Taiwan. According to  the  "Monthly  Revenue  Statistics",  as  published  by  the  Ministry  of  Economic Affairs, the beauty, health and medical supplies retail industry (hereafter referred to as the "medical and cosmetics retail industry") saw steady growth in revenue, with an annual growth rate of 8.3% in 2022, better than the 7.4% for the overall retail industry. Revenues were significantly higher, mainly driven by the high volume of demand for RDT (rapid diagnostic test) from April to June in the second quarter of 2022. The performance in the second half of the year was not as impressive as in the second quarter, but with the pandemic greatly easing and the government's launching of various relevant measures to revitalize the economy, people are returning to their normal outings. The demand for daily cosmetic products, together with the focus on the concept of preventive medicine, has made people more willing to buy preventive health care products than ever before, thus the annual growth rate for this market in December also increased to 9.2%.

## (3) Supply, demand and growth outlook

## A. Supply

The Company operates a chain store of medicare supplies in Taiwan and sits at the downstream  of  the  whole  medicare  supply  chain.  At  the  upstream  are  the manufacturers of pharmaceuticals, medical devices, medical supplies, wellness and biotech products. The downstream players are in direct contact with end consumers. The global market was still affected by the COVID-19 pandemic in the first half of 2022, and the demand for commodities, such as masks, RDT, and thermometers, continued to maintain this peak. However, in the second half of the year, the impact

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

of  the  pandemic  gradually  diminished  and  people  were  returning  to  their  prepandemic routines, resulting in a significant drop in demand for pandemic-related products. According to a report by IEK Consulting, the global medical device market size  reached  US$454.3  billion  in  2021,  an  increase  of  6.3%  from  2020,  and  is estimated to reach US$535.2 billion by 2024. Whilst the medical device market in Taiwan continues to grow, there are challenges ahead with the development of new service  models  post  COVID-19  and  due  to  increasingly  stringent  regulations  on medical devices.

Given  the  higher  awareness  in  health,  population  aging,  low  birth  rates,  it  is  a challenge to meet the ever increasing demand for long-term care and to alleviate the burden of families. The Executive Yuan launched the Long-Term Care Program 2.0 in 2017. Long-term care services have become a priority in the government's control and supervision. All the city/county governments have been pushing for the LongTerm Care Program 2.0. Many peripheral sectors are also beginning to prepare for the  long-term  care  market,  such  as  aassistive  device  services,  home  medicare, dementia care, care services, homecare  and rehabilitation at home  and  in communities. Meanwhile, the sale of medical devices online is allowed in stages. This will open up the retail market and the competitive landscape. Currently, online stores can sell Class I medical devices.

## B.   Demand

## (A) Domestic medical device market

The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Ministry of Interior announced that Taiwan officially entered the aged society in 2018. One out of every seven people is elderly. In face of this heavy burden of one to seven, Medfirst has been dedicated to the gray-haired market and homecare services for nearly 30 years. We sell niche products and provide professional consultation, medical knowledge and education in the use of assistive devices. All these set Medfirst apart  from  its  peers. As  the  percentage  of  aged  population  increases,  the elderly  market  offers  more  and  more  business  opportunities. According  to 'Population Forecast for Republic of China in 2014-2061' produced by the Council for Economic Planning and Development (CEPD), Executive Yuan, the population aged 65 and above will increase from 3,268 thousand in 2017 to 7,152 thousand in 2061. As far as the aged demography is concerned, the percentage of the 65- 74 age group is on a steady decline and the percentage of the 75-85 age group is on a steady increase. In sum, the above 65 years old are accounting a higher percentage of the population in Taiwan. The rising percentage of the above 75 years old reflects the longer life expectancy. The expanding  aged  population  and  the  longer  average  life  expectancy  are prompting consumers to be conscious about living longer, better and healthier. The demand for medicare, healthcare and biotech/wellness products is set to grow. According to Medfirst's membership data, 26.31% are above 60 years old and 49.21% are in the 40-60 age group. This indicates the gray-haired is long-standing clientele for Medfirst and will continue to drive the growth of the industry where we operate.

## (B) Medical device market in China

Given the higher standard of living and the stronger awareness in health in China, the demand for medical devices continues to grow. China's external trade of medical devices has been increasing at nearly 10% each year, higher than the global average growth. Since 2015, the medical device market in China has been growing at 20% per annum and is expected to reach RMB 800 billion by 2020. Both the 12 th and the 13 th Five Year Plans for National Economy and Social Development of the People's Republic of China declare China's determination to develop and promote the medical device industry. As the population aging continues, disposal income per capita increases and the  policy  support  progresses,  the  Chinese  medical  device  industry  shows great growth potential.

## (C) Biotech/wellness food market

The global population aging, increasing health awareness and the emerging of the Asian Pacific market are bringing a new breath of life to the global medicare and healthcare market. A report by Research And Markets forecasts the  global  dietary  supplement  (health  food)  market  to  reach  US$194.63 billion (or NT$5,754.2 billion) by 2025 at a CAGR of 7.8%.

COVID-19 has been speeding up the development of the information age. The public's awareness and the knowledge in diet, wellness and healthcare is increasing. The spenders are getting younger and the business opportunity is tremendous.  The  study  by  the  Industrial  Technology  Research  Institute indicates that the global anti-aging market will reach US$86 billion in 2022. A report from the World Health Organization shows that the population at and above 65 years old will double by 2050. The wellness food market will grow at  a  CAGR of 6.5% in 2017-2022. Nutritional supplements are the largest segment, accounting for 48% of the total. The market size is about US$30.2 billion.

According to a Nielsen survey, 80% of the interviewees said that they will continue to pay attention to a healthy diet after COVID-19. The current focus is  on  better immunity, emotions, sleep, intestinal health, beauty and vision care. Data from Innova Market Insights on the global vision care market in 2017-2019  indicates  the  highest  CAGR  of  20%  for Asia  Pacific.  This  is

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

followed  by  North America  and  Europe,  at  a  CAGR  of  5.3%  and  5.1%, respectively. As  the  demand  for  health  grows,  the  wellness  food  industry welcomes a new stage  of  development.  Continued  innovation  and  precise positioning of wellness foods is the key to product competitiveness in this trend.

- (4) Competitive niche
- A.   Steady customer relations and trust from consumers

We  endeavor  to  become  the  'health  manager  for  your  family'.  The  medical professionalism of our employees is the best in the industry. We provide professional advice and reminders to customers and satisfy customers' needs with sophisticated services.  We  have  built  a  professional  reputation  for  the  Medfirst  brand  by establishing a high level of trust from customers.

- B.   Wide range of products to meet consumers' needs

We have a large network of stores to provide services all over Taiwan. We sell a wide range  of  products  with  professional  services  and  explanations  from  the  medicare team. We provide one-stop shopping experience and we were the first in the industry to  offer  returns,  refunds  or  item  changes  within  seven  days.  We  keep  customers assured by providing a variety of products and comprehensive services.

- C.   Collective bargaining to reduce procurement costs

By leveraging our high market share, we spare no efforts in quality control and cost reduction of procured goods, in order to serve as a gatekeeper for customers and return to customers.

- D.   Centered on medicare supplies and services and extension to hospital stores

We also provide turnkey solutions to hospital stores by extending various and indepth services to all aspects of life. As the health manager for your family, we are everywhere and we contribute to the quality of life for citizens.

- E.    Roots in Taiwan and footprint overseas

Anchored on our experience with the Taiwan market and medical professionalism, we have entered the China market early to capture the trend in development.

- (5) Positive factors, negative factors and responding strategy for future developments
- A.   Positive factors
3. (A) Taiwan  government's  drive  for  the  development  of  the  medical  device industry

The biotech industry in Taiwan consists of four sectors, i.e., pharmaceuticals, medical  devices,  applied  biotech,  and  health/wellness. As  the  technology advances and develops, the new drugs and medical devices developed by the biotech  industry  in  Taiwan  have  been  widely  recognized  by  the  U.S.,  the European Union and Japan. This has attracted many international business opportunities and attention to the medical device market. A report from BMI Research suggests that the global market of medical devices totaled US$454.3 billion  in  2021  and  is  forecasted  to  reach  US$535.2  billion  in  2024,  at  a CAGR of 5.6% or so in 2022~2025. Meanwhile, the international regulations on medical devices have changed rapidly during recent years and the review

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

and  supervision  on  medical  devices  have  become  increasingly  stringent. Hence, the Taiwan government has been proactively educating and nurturing regulatory talents to address the demand from the medical device industry. This  helps  the  manufacturers  in  the  development  of  medical  devices  and drives the continued industry growth.

Against the backdrop of the policies and topical events, the demand from the National Health Insurance system and the Long-Term Care Program 2.0 in Taiwan  underpins  the  development  of  the  medical  device  market. As  the population ages, the medicare demand for chronical diseases is rising year over  year.  The  stable  long-term  growth  is  set  to  encourage  a  plethora  of innovative products and market opportunities for Taiwan's medical device industry.

- (B) Increase in national incomes, aged population percentage and awareness for health and wellness

Given the continued increase of national incomes, aged population percentage and average life expectancy in Taiwan, the public is becoming more and more awareness of health and wellness in order to live longer, better and healthier. The expenditures on medical treatment and prevention is expected to continue growing due to the demand for health/wellness, chronic diseases and longterm  patient  care.  This  will  drive  the  growth  momentum  of  the  medical supplies market.

- (C) Continued increase in the number of stores and deepening of channel efforts as a leader in the medicare supplies retail market

We are the leader in the domestic medicare supplies retail market measured with the number of stores. We have a good brand, image and reputation and we  have  established  many  directly  owned  stores  and  presence  in  hospital stores in Taiwan. Our stores are all in the prime locations within and close to hospitals. We also undertake and operate the stores within hospitals. Going forward,  we  will  continue  to  increase  the  number  of  stores  and  develop channels. We will expand the menu of products and services in Taiwan and continue to grow the medical supplies business in China, in order to create the benefits of scale and a critical mass.

- (D) Development of own label products based on the understanding of customers' needs and preferences, in order to enhance  services and customers' satisfaction

The Company operates a professional chain store of medical supplies. Due to the  industry  characteristics,  we  are  in  direct  contact  with  consumers  and understand the needs and preferences of customers. This allows us to develop products of our own label to cater to customers' requirements. By selling the products  better  suited  to  consumers,  we  boost  customers'  satisfaction  and increase repeated purchases.

- (E) Effective contribution to revenues from high brand loyalty and stickiness of member customers

Our store personnel invites members for repeated purchases and promotional campaigns,  to  boost  in-store  traffic  and  strengthen  the  brand  loyalty  and stickiness of customers. Currently, we have more than 2.97 million members.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

As our members enjoy discounts by presenting membership cards and can use bonus points as cash and receive birthday gifts, they are encouraged to come back and shop more. More than half of our current monthly revenues come from members and this percentage continues to climb up. This indicates the high loyalty and stickiness of our member customers to our brand and channel. Member  customers  are  expected  to  contribute  to  a  higher  share  of  our revenues and to our growth momentum.

- B.   Negative factors and responding strategies
2. (A) Growing competitive intensity due to lines blurring between industries

Given the increasing aging in developed countries and higher growth in the gray-haired LOHAS segment compared to other markets, drugstores, beauty and  health  retailers  and  ecommerce  platforms  are  starting  to  sell  medical supplies. The blurring lines between industries will intensify the competition for products and prices.

## Responding strategy:

We endeavor to train and develop the professional knowledge and service enthusiasm of our store personnel, so that they have a good and proactive attitude in providing answers to customers regarding healthcare and medical supplies. With comprehensive and professional services, we offer the most suited  and  complete  medicare  supplies  and  solutions.  This  enhances  the recognition, trust and loyalty of customers to our brand and channel.

In  addition,  we  establish  strategic  partnerships  with  agents  in  different locations  in  order  to  understand  market  trends  and  provide  differentiated functions, price competitive strategies, brand marketing capabilities and total solutions. This maintains long-term stable collaboration and cooperation in market creation.

- (B) Difficulty in quality control due to a large product variety and a wide span of management

In  the  spirit  of  servicing  customers,  we  sell  a  large  mix  and  diversity  of products.  The  high  number  of  suppliers  makes  product  quality  control relatively difficult.

## Responding strategy:

Before bringing a product to the store shelf, we strengthen the quality control and  assess  the  rating  of  the  supplier.  This  is  a  proactive  and  preventive measure to control product quality for customers. In event of product defects, we identify and recall these products so that our customers do not end up buying the problematic items. This enhances the customers' confidence in our company.

- (C) Our brand and image not well known in China

As a believer of the market potential in China, we have been developing the Chinese market for years. However, the spending behaviors and methods in China are different from those in Taiwan. In addition, local competitors have home advantages and abundant capital in this vast country. As a result, it is difficult for our company to build the brand and publicity. Our business in

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

China did not meet our expectations despite significant growth.

## Responding strategy:

As the premier brand from Taiwan, the Company hopes to gradually expand presence and develop channels and the brand name in Shanghai, Nanjing, Xiamen, Hangzhou and Beijing where purchasing power is relatively high. By complementing our product portfolio and strengthening sale skills in-store and  supported  with  our  love,  caring  and  patient,  as  well  as  sincerity  and satisfaction with customers, we strive to enhance the customers' recognition for our brand in our gradual efforts in the China market. Hopefully this will boost the overall operating performance.

## (3) Employee retirement system

The Company attributes funds according to the relevant pension system, and employees can  enjoy  various  social  security  benefits  after  retirement. Employees  who  apply  for  retirement  in  accordance  with  the  separation  management regulations are allowed to go through the handover operation after being interviewed and approved by the supervisor in charge; then the Human Resources Division confirms that all  retirement  procedures  have  been  completed,  settles  the  salary,  and  retains  the information in the Human Resources Division.

## VI. Information Security Management

In order to ensure the safety of business operations and consumer rights, we established the "Information Security Management Committee of Medfirst Healthcare Services" in December 2019, and set up this information security management policy as the highest guiding principle.

- (1)    Framework of Information Security Risk Management

## (2) Information security policy

- (a) Establishment of management  rules and regulations: To establish relevant information security management rules and regulations in compliance with laws and  to  provide  appropriate  protection  measures  for  the  Company's  information assets to ensure their availability, confidentiality, and integrity.
- (b) Impact response plan: To regularly evaluate the impact of various man-made and natural disasters on the Company's information assets, and to formulate disaster prevention  and  recovery  plans  for  important  information  assets  to  ensure  the continuous operations of the Company's business.
- (c) Strengthening of information security awareness: To supervise employees' implementation of information security protection in the company, and enhance the awareness of information security among department heads and employees.
- (d) Implementation of information security regulations: To advise all employees of the Company and  the  clients  they  work  with  to  comply  with  information  securityrelated  regulations,  and  in  case  of  non-compliance,  they  are  subject  to  the Company's regulations or contractual penalties.

This policy shall be implemented after being reviewed and resolved by the Information Security  Management  Committee  and  audited  by  president,  and  the  same  applies  to

<!-- image -->

amendments.

This policy shall be evaluated and reviewed at least once a year, taking into account the latest status of laws and regulations, technological changes, expectations of concerned parties,  business  activities,  internal  management  and  resources,  etc.,  to  ensure  the effectiveness of information security practices.

## **The formulas for calculating the financial ratio are as follows:

1. Capital Structure
- (1) Liabilities to assets ratio = total liabilities / total assets
- (2) Long-term funds to property, plant and equipment ratio = (total equity + non-current liabilities) / net property, plant and equipment
2. Liquidity
- (1)   Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities
- (2)   Quick ratio = (current assets - inventory- prepaid expenses) / current liabilities
- (3)   Interest coverage ratio (times) = net gains before income tax and interest / interest expenses of the current term
3. Operating ability
- (1)   Account receivables (including Notes receivables from operating activities and accounts receivable) turnover = net sales/average receivables of each term (including notes receivables from operating activities and accounts receivable) balance
- (2)   Average days of accounts receivable = 365 / receivables turnover rate
- (3)   Inventory turnover rate = COGS (cost of goods sold)/average inventory amount
- (4)   Account  payables  (including  Notes  payable  from  operating  activities  and  accounts  payable) turnover= COGS (cost of goods sold)/average payables of each term (including Notes payable from operating activities and accounts payable) balance
- (5)   Average days of sales = 365 / inventory turnover rate
- (6)   Property, plant and equipment turnover rate = net sales / average net property, factory and equipment
- (7)   Total assets turnover rate = net sales / average total assets
4. Profitability
- (1)   Return on assets = [gain/loss after tax + interest expense x (1-tax rate)] / average total asset
- (2)   Return on equity = gain/loss after tax / average total equity
- (3)   Net margin = gain/loss after tax / net sales
- (4)   Earnings  per  share  =  (net  profit  after  tax  -  preferred  stock  dividend)  /  weighted  average  shares outstanding (Note 4)
5. Cash flow
- (1)   Operating cash flow ratio = net cash flow of operating activities/current liabilities
- (2)   Cash flow adequacy ratio= net cash flow of operating activities in the past five years / the past five years sum of (capital expenditures + inventory addition +cash dividends)
- (3)   Cash reinvestment ratio= (net cash flow of operating activities- cash dividends) / (Property, plant and equipment gross + long term investment + other non-current assets + working capital) (Note 5)
6. Leverage
- (1)   Operating leverage = (operating revenues - variable operating cost and expenses)/operating income (Noe 6)
- (2)   Financial leverage = operating profit / (operating profit - interest expense)

Analysis of changes in percentage of increase/decrease (for changes of 20% or more in the prior and subsequent periods, with amounts exceeding NT$10 million or more):

1. Increase in other assets: Mainly due to that newly developed stores and large marketplaces and stores are recorded as right-of-use assets and investment property in this period, as the result of the application of IFRS 16.
2. Decrease  in  long-term  liabilities:  Mainly  due  to  that  the  holders  of  convertible  corporate  bonds  are successively converting these bonds into the Company's common stock, with the recording date for the sale of convertible corporate bonds listed as March 2, 2023, which is then recorded as current liabilities within one year.
3. Increase  in  other  liabilities:  Mainly  due  to  the  newly  developed  stores  and  large  marketplaces  being recorded as leasing liabilities, as a result of the application of IFRS16.
4. Increase in retained earnings: Mainly due to a 10.46% increase in operating revenues, maintaining a 30% gross profit margin, while controlling the expense ratio, which resulted in a significant increase in net income for the period, as compared to the previous period.
5. Increase in other equity: This is due to the changes in the conversion differences of foreign operating institutions for the year.
