## Amendment to IAS 1 "Classification of liabilities as current or non-current' (amended in 2020) and "Non-current liabilities with covenants" (amended in 2022)

The 2020 amendment is to determine whether, in determining whether a liability is classified as noncurrent, the Group should assess whether it has the right to defer settlement until at least 12 months after the end of the reporting period. If the Group has  such  a  right  as  of  the  end  of  the  reporting  period,  the  liability  is  classified  as noncurrent regardless of whether the Group expects to exercise the right.

The 2020 amendments also provide that if the Group is required to comply with certain conditions in order to have the right to defer settlement of a liability, the Group shall have complied with the specified conditions as of the end of the reporting period, even if the lender tests whether the Group has complied with those conditions at a later date. The 2022 amendments further clarify that only contractual terms that are required to be met prior to the end of the reporting period will affect the classification of the liability.  Contractual  terms  that  are  required  to  be  met  within  12  months  after  the reporting period do not affect the classification of the liability, but are required to be disclosed so that users of financial reports are aware of the risk that the Group may not be  able  to  comply  with  the  contractual  terms  and  be  required  to  make  repayments within 12 months after the reporting period.

The 2020 amendment provides that for the purpose of liability classification, the aforementioned settlement refers to the extinguishment of a liability resulting from the transfer of cash, other economic resources or equity instruments of the Group to the counterparty. However, if a liability may be settled by transferring an equity instrument of a Group at the option of the counterparty, and if the option is separately recognized in  equity  in  accordance  with  IAS  32,  "Financial  Instruments:  Presentation,"  the aforementioned provision does not affect the classification of the liability.

As of the publication date of this Consolidated Financial Report, the Group is still evaluating the impact of the amendments to other standards and interpretations on its financial  position  and  financial  performance,  which  will  be  disclosed  upon  the completion of assessment.

## IV. Summary Description of Major Accounting Policies

## (I) Compliance declaration

This Consolidated Financial Report has been prepared in accordance with Standards for Preparation of Financial Report by Securities Issuers and IFRSs approved and issued by the FSC.

## (II) Preparation basis

The Consolidated Financial Report is prepared on a historical cost basis, except for the financial instruments measured at fair value and the net defined benefit liability recognized at present value of defined benefit obligation minus fair value of plan asset.

Fair-value measurements are classified into Level 1 to 3 according to the observable degree and importance of relevant input values:

1.    Level 1 input value: the (unadjusted) quotation in active markets for identical asset or liability available at the measurement date.
2.    Level 2 input value: the observable input value of asset or liability, either directly (i.e., price) or indirectly (i.e., derived from price), in addition to the quotation in Level 1.
3.    Level 3 input value: the unobservable input value of asset or liability.

## (III) Classification of Current and Noncurrent Assets and Liabilities

Current assets include

1.    Assets held primarily for trading purposes;
2.    Assets expected to be realized within 12 months after the balance sheet date; and
3.    Cash  and  cash  equivalents  (excluding  those  restricted  for  exchange  or  settlement  of liabilities more than 12 months after the balance sheet date).

Current liabilities include:

1.    Liabilities held primarily for trading purposes;
2.    Liabilities that are due for settlement within 12 months after the balance sheet date, and
3.    Liabilities for which the maturity date cannot be unconditionally extended to at least 12 months after the balance sheet date.

Assets and liabilities that are not current assets or current liabilities as described above are classified as noncurrent assets or noncurrent liabilities.

## (IV) Consolidation basis

This Consolidated Financial Report contains the financial statements of the Company and the entities  (subsidiaries)  controlled  by  the  Company.  The  consolidated  statements  of comprehensive income have included the operating profit and loss of the acquired or disposed subsidiary for the current period from the date of acquisition or up to the date of disposal. The financial reports of subsidiaries have been adjusted to bring the accounting policies in line with those  of  the  Group.  At  the  time  of  preparation  of  the  Consolidated  Financial  Report,  all transactions,  account  balances,  profits,  expenses  and  losses  between  the  entities  have  been written  off.  The  total  comprehensive  incomes  of  the  subsidiaries  are  attributable  to  the Company's owners and non-controlling interests, even though the non-controlling interests have become a deficit balance.

When the change in the Group's ownership interest in a subsidiary does not result in a loss of control, it shall be treated as an equity transaction. The carrying amounts of the Group and non-controlling interests have been adjusted to reflect the changes in their relative interests in the subsidiaries. The difference between the amount of adjustment of the non-controlling interest and the fair value of the consideration paid or received is recognized directly in equity and belongs to the owners of the Company.

For details of subsidiaries, shareholding ratio and operating items, see Note XII, Schedules 5 and 6.

## (V) Foreign currencies

When preparing financial statements, each entity records transactions in currencies other than the functional currency of the entity (foreign currencies) in its functional currency at the exchange rate prevailing on the transaction date.

Monetary items denominated in foreign currencies are translated at the closing rate at each balance sheet date. Exchange differences arising from the settlement of monetary items or the translation of monetary items are recognized in profit or loss in the period in which they occur.

Non-monetary items measured at fair value that are denominated in foreign currencies are translated at the exchange rates prevailing on the date when the fair value was determined, and the resulting exchange differences are included in profit or loss for the current period. However, if a change in fair value is recognized in other comprehensive income, the resulting exchange differences are included in other comprehensive income.

Non-monetary items denominated in foreign currencies that are measured at historical cost are  translated  at  the  exchange  rates  prevailing  on  the  dates  of  transactions  and  are  not retranslated.

For  the  purpose  of  preparing  consolidated  financial  statements,  assets  and  liabilities  of foreign operations (including subsidiaries that operate in countries or currencies different from those of the Company) are translated into New Taiwan dollars at the exchange rates prevailing on each balance sheet date. Income and expense items are translated at the average exchange rates for the period, with the resulting exchange differences recognized in other comprehensive income (and attributed to the Company's owners and non-controlling interests, respectively).

If the Group disposes of all the interests in a foreign operation, or disposes of part of the interests in a subsidiary of a foreign operation but loses control, or if the retained interests after the disposal of an affiliate of a foreign operation are financial assets and are accounted for under the accounting policy for financial instruments, all cumulative exchange differences attributable to the Company's owners and related to the foreign operation are reclassified to profit or loss.

## (VI) Inventories

Inventories are commodity inventories. Inventories are measured at the lower of cost or net realizable value. Comparisons between cost and net realizable value are made on an item-byitem basis, except for similar inventories. Net realizable value is the estimated selling price under normal circumstances, less any remaining selling expenses. The cost of inventories is calculated using the weighted-average method.

## (VII)  Property, plant and equipment

Property, plant and equipment are recognized at cost and subsequently measured at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses.

Property,  plant  and  equipment,  except  for  owned  land,  which  is  not  depreciated,  are depreciated separately for each significant portion of the property, plant and equipment over their useful lives on a straight-line basis. The Group reviews the estimated useful lives, residual values and depreciation methods at least at each year-end and defers the effect of changes in applicable accounting estimates.

When property,  plant  and  equipment  are  derecognized,  the  difference  between  the  net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset is recognized in profit or loss.

## (VIII) Investment Properties

Investment properties are real estate (including right-to-use assets that meet the definition of investment properties) held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation or both. Investment properties also include land held that is currently undecided as to its future use.

Owned investment properties are initially measured at cost (including transaction costs) and subsequently measured at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses.

Investment properties acquired under leases are initially measured at cost (including the original measurement of the lease liability, lease payments made before the commencement date of the lease, the original direct cost and the estimated cost of restoration of the subject asset, less lease incentives received) and subsequently measured at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses, and the remeasurement of the lease liability is adjusted.

All investment properties are depreciated on a straight-line basis.

When investment  properties  are  derecognized,  the  difference  between  the  net  disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the assets is recognized in profit or loss.

## (IX) Goodwill

Goodwill acquired in an acquisition of a business is measured at cost based on the amount of  goodwill  recognized  at  the  acquisition  date  and  subsequently  measured  at  cost  less accumulated impairment losses.

For the purposes of impairment testing, goodwill is allocated to each cash-generating unit or group of cash-generating units ("cash-generating units ") of the Group that is expected to benefit from the synergies of the combination.

A cash-generating unit to which goodwill is allocated is tested for impairment annually (and whenever there is an indication that the unit may be impaired) by comparing the carrying amount of the unit containing goodwill with its recoverable amount. If goodwill is allocated to a cash-generating unit as a result of a business combination in the current year, the unit should be tested for impairment before the end of the current year. If the recoverable amount of the cash-generating  unit  to  which  goodwill  is  allocated  is  less  than  its  carrying  amount,  the impairment loss reduces the carrying amount of the goodwill allocated to the cash-generating unit first and then reduces the carrying amount of each asset in proportion to the carrying amount of the other assets in the unit. Any impairment loss is recognized directly as a loss in the current period. An impairment loss on goodwill is not reversed in subsequent periods.

Upon disposal of an operation within the cash generating unit to which goodwill is allocated, the  amount  of  goodwill  associated  with  the  disposed  operation  is  included  in  the  carrying amount of the operation to determine the gain or loss on disposal.

## (X) Intangible assets

## 1. Separate Acquisitions

Separately acquired intangible assets with finite useful lives are initially measured at cost and subsequently measured at cost less accumulated amortization and accumulated impairment losses. Intangible assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over their useful lives.  The  Group  reviews  the  estimated  useful  lives,  residual  values  and  amortization methods at least at each year-end and defers the effect of changes in applicable accounting estimates.

## 2. Derecognition

When an intangible asset is  derecognized,  the  difference  between the  net  disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset is recognized in profit or loss for the current period.

## (XI) Impairment of Property, Plant and Equipment, Right-of-Use Assets, Investment Property and Assets Related to Intangible Assets (Other Than Goodwill)

The Group assesses at each balance sheet date whether there is any indication that property, plant  and  equipment,  right-of-use  assets  and  intangible  assets  (other  than  goodwill)  may  be impaired. If any indication of impairment exists, the recoverable amount of the asset is estimated.

If the recoverable amount of an individual asset cannot be estimated, the Group estimates the recoverable amount of the cash-generating unit to which the asset belongs.

The recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use. If the recoverable amount of an individual asset or cash-generating unit is less than its carrying amount, the carrying amount of the asset or cash-generating unit is reduced to its recoverable amount, and the impairment loss is recognized in profit or loss.

When an impairment loss is subsequently reversed, the carrying amount of the asset or cash-generating  unit  is  increased  to  the  revised  recoverable  amount.  However,  the  revised carrying amount is not to exceed the carrying amount (net of amortization or depreciation) that would  have  been  determined  had  the  asset  or  cash-generating  unit  not  recognized  the impairment loss in prior years. Reversal of impairment loss is recognized in profit or loss.

## (XII)  Non-current assets held for sale

The carrying amount of a noncurrent asset is classified as held for sale when the asset is expected to be recovered principally through a sale transaction rather than through continued use. Non-current assets that are classified as such must be available for immediate sale in their current condition and their sale must be highly probable. A sale is considered highly probable when the appropriate level of management has committed to a plan to sell the asset and the sale transaction is expected to be completed within one year from the date of classification.

Non-current assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell, and depreciation on such assets is discontinued.

## (XIII) Financial instruments

Financial assets and financial liabilities are recognized in the consolidated balance sheet when the Group becomes a party to the contractual provisions of the instrument.

On initial recognition of financial assets and financial liabilities, if the financial assets or financial liabilities are not measured at fair value through profit or loss, they are measured at fair value plus transaction costs that are directly attributable to the acquisition or issuance of the financial assets or financial liabilities. Transaction costs directly attributable to the acquisition or issuance of financial assets or financial liabilities measured at fair value through profit or loss are recognized immediately in profit or loss.

## 1. Financial Assets

Regular transactions of financial assets are recognized and derecognized on a trade date basis.

## (1) Categories of measurement

The  financial  assets  held  by  the  Group  are  classified  as  financial  assets measured at fair value through profit or loss, financial assets measured at amortized cost,  and  investments  in  equity  instruments  measured  at  fair  value  through  other comprehensive income.

## A. Financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss

Financial  assets  measured  at  fair  value  through  profit  or  loss  include financial assets that are mandatorily measured at fair value through profit or loss. Financial assets mandatorily measured at fair value through profit or loss include investments in equity instruments that are not designated as at fair value through other comprehensive  income, and investments in debt instruments that do not qualify for classification as measured at amortized cost or at fair value through other comprehensive income.

Financial  assets  measured  at  fair  value  through  profit  or  loss  are measured at fair value, with remeasurement gains or losses recognized in other gains  and  losses.  For  the  determination  of  fair  value,  please  refer  to  Note XXXIV.

## B. Financial assets measured at amortized cost

The  Group's  investments  in  financial  assets  are  classified  as  financial assets measured at amortized cost if both of the following two conditions are met:

- a. They are held under an operating model whose objective is to hold the financial assets to collect the contractual cash flows; and
- b. The contractual terms give rise to cash flows at a specific date, which are solely  payments  of  principal  and  interest  on  the  principal  amount outstanding.

After  initial  recognition,  financial  assets  measured  at  amortized  cost (including cash and cash equivalents, notes receivable, accounts receivable, other  receivables  and  refundable  deposits  measured  at  amortized  cost)  are measured at their amortized cost after deducting any impairment loss from their total carrying amount determined by the effective interest method, with any gain or loss on foreign currency exchange recognized in profit or loss.

Interest income is calculated by multiplying the effective interest rate by the total carrying amount of the financial asset, except for the following two circumstances:

- a. For acquired or created credit-impaired financial assets, interest income is calculated by multiplying the credit-adjusted effective interest rate by the amortized cost of the financial asset.
- b. For credit-impaired financial assets that are not acquired or created but subsequently  become  credit-impaired, interest income  is  computed by multiplying  the  effective  interest  rate  by  the  amortized  cost  of  the financial assets from the next reporting period after the impairment is applied.

Credit-impaired  financial  assets  are  those  for  which  the  issuer  or  the debtor  has  experienced  significant  financial  difficulties,  defaulted,  or  it  is probable that the debtor will declare bankruptcy or other financial reorganization or that an active market for the financial assets will disappear due to financial difficulties.

Cash equivalents include time deposits within 3 months from the date of acquisition, which are highly liquid, readily convertible to a fixed amount of cash and subject to insignificant risk of changes in value, and are used to meet short-term cash commitments.

- C. Investments  in  equity  instruments  measured  at  fair  value  through  other comprehensive income

At initial recognition, the Group has an irrevocable option to designate investments  in  equity  instruments  that  are  not  held-for-trading  and  not recognized by a business combination acquirer as contingent consideration to be measured at fair value through other comprehensive income.

Investments in equity instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income are measured at fair value, with subsequent changes in fair  value  recognized  in  other  comprehensive  income  and  accumulated  in other equity. Upon disposal of such investments, the cumulative gain or loss is transferred directly to retained earnings and is not reclassified to profit or loss.

Dividends from investments in equity instruments measured at fair value through other comprehensive income are recognized in profit or loss when the

Group's right to receive the dividends is established, unless it is clear that the dividends represent a partial recovery of the cost of the investment.

## (2) Impairment of financial assets

The Group assesses financial assets (including accounts receivable) measured at amortized cost based on expected credit losses at each balance sheet date.

Allowance  for accounts receivable and operating lease receivables are recognized on the basis of expected credit losses over the duration. Other financial assets are evaluated to determine whether there is a significant increase in credit risk since  initial  recognition.  If  there  is  no  significant  increase,  loss  allowance  is recognized on the basis of 12-month expected credit loss, and if there is a significant increase, loss allowance is recognized on the basis of expected credit loss over the duration.

Expected credit losses are the weighted-average credit losses weighted by the risk of default. 12-month expected credit losses represent expected credit losses on financial  instruments  arising  from  possible  defaults  within  12  months  after  the publication date of the financial statements, while expected credit losses over the duration of the financial instruments represent expected credit losses on all possible defaults over the expected duration of the financial instruments.

For  the  purpose  of  internal  credit  risk  management,  the  Group  determines, without regard to the collateral held, that a default on a financial asset has occurred in the following circumstances:

- A. There is internal or external information indicating that the debtor is unlikely to settle the debt.
- B. The financial asset is more than 180 days past due, unless there is reasonable and probable information that a deferred basis of default is more appropriate.

The  carrying  amount  of  financial  assets  impaired  is  reduced  through  an allowance  account.  However,  the  allowance  for  losses  on  investments  in  debt instruments  measured  at  fair  value  through  other  comprehensive  income  is recognized in other comprehensive income and does not reduce the carrying amount of those instruments.

## (3) Derecognition of financial assets

The Group derecognizes financial assets only when the contractual rights to the cash flows from the financial assets expire or when the financial assets have been transferred and substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership of the assets have been transferred to other enterprises.

When a financial asset measured at amortized cost is derecognized in its entirety, the  difference  between  the  carrying  amount  and  the  consideration  received  is recognized in profit or loss. When investments in debt instruments measured at fair value  through  other  comprehensive  income  are  derecognized  as  a  whole,  the difference between the carrying amount and the sum of the consideration received plus  any  cumulative  gain  or  loss  recognized  in  other  comprehensive  income  is recognized  in  profit  or  loss.  When  investments  in  equity  instruments  that  are measured at fair value through other comprehensive income are derecognized as a whole, the cumulative gain or loss is transferred directly to retained earnings and is not reclassified to profit or loss.

## 2. Equity instruments

Debt and equity instruments issued by the Group are classified as financial liabilities or  equity  based  on  the  substance  of  the  contractual  agreements  and  the  definitions  of financial liabilities and equity instruments.

Equity instruments issued by the Group are recognized at the amount of the proceeds received less direct issuance costs.

Redemptions of the Group's own equity instruments are recognized and derecognized under equity, and their carrying amounts are calculated based on the weighted-average number of shares. The purchase, sale, issuance or cancellation of the Company's own equity instruments are not recognized in profit or loss.

## 3. Financial liabilities

## (1) Subsequent measurement

All  financial  liabilities  are  measured  at  amortized  cost  using  the  effective interest method, except for the following:

## Financial liabilities measured at fair value through profit or loss

Financial liabilities measured at fair value through profit or loss include those held-for-trading

Financial liabilities  held-for-trading  are  measured at fair  value, and  gains  or losses arising from their remeasurement are recognized in other gains and losses.

For the determination of fair value, please refer to Note XXXIV.

## (2) Derecognition of financial liabilities

When a financial liability is derecognized, the difference between the carrying amount and  the  consideration  paid  (including  any  non-cash  assets  transferred  or liabilities assumed) is recognized in profit or loss.

## 4. Convertible corporate bonds

The  Group's  compound  financial  instruments  (convertible  corporate  bonds)  are classified as financial liabilities and equity components upon initial recognition based on the substance of the contractual agreements and the definitions of financial liabilities and equity instruments, respectively.

At initial recognition, the fair value of the liability component is estimated using the prevailing market interest rate for a similar non-convertible instrument and is measured at amortized cost using the effective interest method before the date of conversion or maturity. Liability  components that are  embedded in  non-equity  derivatives  are  measured  at  fair value.

The conversion right classified as equity is equal to the remaining amount of the fair value of the compound instrument as a whole less the fair value of the liability component determined separately and is recognized in equity, net of income tax effects, and is not subsequently  measured.  When  the  conversion  right  is  exercised,  the  related  liability component and the amount in equity will be reclassified to stock capital and capital surplusissuance premium. If the conversion right of the convertible bonds is not exercised on the maturity  date,  the  amount  recognized  in  equity  will  be  reclassified  to  capital  surplus  issuance premium.

Transaction  costs  related  to  the  issuance  of  convertible  bonds  are  allocated  to  the liability  component  (included  in  the  carrying  amount  of  the  liability)  and  the  equity component (included in equity) of the instrument in proportion to the total allocated price.

## 5. Derivative instruments

The  derivative  instruments  entered  into  by  the  Group  include  call/put  rights  and conversion options.

Derivative  instruments  are  recognized  at  fair  value  initially  when  the  derivative contracts are entered into and subsequently remeasured at fair value on the balance sheet date, with gains or losses arising from subsequent measurements recognized directly in

profit or loss. When the fair value of a derivative is positive, it is classified as a financial asset; when the fair value is negative, it is classified as a financial liability.

A  derivative  embedded  in  an  asset  master  contract  within  the  scope  of  IFRS  9 "Financial Instruments" is classified as a financial asset based on the contract as a whole. A derivative not embedded in an asset master contract within the scope of IFRS 9 (e.g. embedded in a financial liability master contract) is classified as a separate derivative if the embedded derivative meets the definition of a derivative, the risks and characteristics of which are not closely related to those of the master contract, and the hybrid contract is not measured at fair value through profit or loss.

## (XIV) Provision for liabilities

The  amount  recognized  as  a  provision  for  liabilities,  including  contractual  obligations arising from service concession agreements that specifically state that infrastructure is to be maintained or restored prior to its return to the grantor as well as various types of proceeds legally collected by the government, is the best estimate of the amount required to settle the obligation at the balance sheet date, taking into account the risk and uncertainty of the obligation. The provision for liabilities is measured at the discounted cash flows to settle the obligations.

## (XV)  Revenue Recognition

After the Group identifies performance obligations in customer contracts, the transaction price  is  allocated  to  each  performance  obligation,  and  revenue  is  recognized  when  each performance obligation is satisfied.

## 1. Revenue from sale of goods

Revenue  from  sale  of  goods  is  derived  from  the  sale  of  medical  supplies.  The Company recognizes revenue and accounts receivable at the point of delivery because the customer has the right to use the goods and bears the risk of loss or damage of the goods upon delivery of the medical supplies to the customer.

## 2. Revenue from leases

The Group's investment property is  held  for  the  purpose  of  earning  lease  income. Lease income is  recognized  on  a  straight-line  basis  over  the  period  in  which  the  lease contracts are realized.

## (XVI) Leases

The Group assesses whether the contract is (or contains) a lease at the establishment date of the contract.

## 1. The Group is the lessor

A lease is classified as a finance lease when the terms of the lease transfer substantially all the risks and rewards incidental to ownership of the asset to the lessee. All other leases are classified as operating leases.

When the Group subleases a right-of-use asset, the classification of the sublease is determined by the right-of-use asset (not the subject asset). However, if the master lease is a  short-term  lease  to  which  the  Group applies  a  recognition  exemption, the  sublease is classified as an operating lease.

Under operating leases,  lease  payments,  net  of  lease  incentives,  are  recognized  as income on a straight-line basis over the term of the relevant lease.

Variable rent under leases that do not vary with indices or rates are recognized as incomes in the period in which they are incurred.

When  a  lease  includes  both  land  and  building  elements,  the  Group  assesses  the classification of each element as a finance or operating lease based on whether substantially all the risks and rewards incidental to the ownership of each element have been transferred to the lessee. Lease payments are allocated to land and buildings in proportion to the fair

value of the leasehold rights to the land and buildings at the establishment date of the contract. If lease payments can be reliably allocated to these two elements, each element is treated in accordance with the applicable lease classification. If the lease payments cannot be reliably allocated to these two elements, the entire lease is classified as a finance lease, but  if  both  elements  clearly  meet  the  criteria  for  an  operating  lease,  the  entire  lease  is classified as an operating lease.

## 2. The Group is the lessee

Except for leases of low-value subject assets to which recognition exemptions apply and short-term leases where lease payments are recognized as expenses on a straight-line basis over the lease term, the right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized for all other leases on the commencement date of the lease.

Right-of-use assets are measured initially at cost (including the original measurement of the lease liability, lease payments made prior to the commencement date of the lease less lease incentives received, original direct cost and estimated cost of restoration of the subject asset) and subsequently measured at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses, and the remeasurement of the lease liability is adjusted. Except for those assets  that  meet  the  definition  of  investment  property,  right-of-use  assets  are  presented separately in the consolidated balance sheet. For the recognition and measurement of rightof-use  assets  that  meet  the  definition  of  investment  property,  please  refer  to  (VIII) Accounting Policies for Investment Property.

Right-of-use assets are depreciated on a straight-line basis from the lease commencement date to the earlier of the end of the useful life or the end of the lease term.

Lease  liabilities  are  measured  initially  at  the  present  value  of  the  lease  payments (including fixed payments). If the interest rate implicit in the lease is readily determinable, the  lease  payments  are  discounted  using  that  rate.  If  such  interest  rate  is  not  readily determinable, the lessee's incremental borrowing rate is used.

Subsequently,  lease  liabilities  are  measured  at  amortized  cost  using  the  effective interest method, and interest expense is allocated over the lease term. If a change in the lease term results in a change in future lease payments, the Group remeasures the lease liability and adjusts the right-of-use asset accordingly, but if the carrying amount of the right-of-use asset is reduced to zero, the remaining remeasurement amount is recognized in  profit  or  loss.  For  lease  modifications  that  are  not  treated  as  separate  leases,  the remeasurement  of  the  lease  liability  due  to  a  reduction  in  the  scope  of  the  lease  is  a reduction of the right-of-use asset and a gain or loss on partial or full termination of the lease is recognized; the remeasurement of the lease liability due to other modifications is an  adjustment  to  the  right-of-use  asset.  Lease  liabilities  are  presented  separately  in  the consolidated balance sheet.

The Group entered into rent reductions directly related to COVID-19 with lessors to adjust payments due prior to July 31, 2024, resulting in a decrease in rental expense and no material change in other lease terms and conditions. The Group chose to adopt a practical expedient approach to all lease reductions that meet the aforementioned criteria. Instead of evaluating whether they are lease modifications, the Group recognized reductions in lease payments in profit or loss (recorded as a reduction of lease costs and operating expenses for changes in lease payments) when the reduction occurs, with a corresponding reduction in lease liabilities.

Variable rent under leases that do not vary with indices or rates are recognized as expenses in the period in which they are incurred.

## (XVII)  Borrowing Costs

Borrowing costs directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of a qualifying asset are included as part of the cost of the asset until substantially all of the activities necessary to bring the asset to its intended use or sale condition have been completed.

Investment income earned on specific borrowings that are temporarily invested prior to the incurrence of qualifying capital expenditures is deducted from the cost of borrowings eligible for capitalization.

Except for the above, all other borrowing costs are recognized in profit or loss in the period in which they are incurred.

## (XVIII) Government grants

Government grants are recognized only when there is reasonable assurance that the Group will comply with the conditions required by the government grant and that the grant will be received.

Government grants related to revenues are recognized in other income on a systematic basis over the period in which the government intends to reimburse the related costs recognized as expenses by the Group. Government grants that are contingent upon the Company's acquisition, construction or other acquisition of non-current assets are recognized as deferred revenue and are transferred to profit or loss on a reasonable and systematic basis over the useful lives of the related assets.

## (XIX) Employee Benefits

## 1. Short-term employee benefits

The liability related to short-term employee benefits is measured at the non-discounted amount expected to be paid in exchange for employee services.

## 2. Post-employment benefits

The defined contribution pension plan is a defined benefit plan in which the amount of pension benefits to be contributed is recognized as an expense over the period of service rendered by the employees.

The defined benefit cost (including service cost, net interest and remeasurement) of the defined benefit pension plan is actuarially calculated using the projected unit credit method. Service cost (including current service cost) and net interest on the net defined benefit liability (asset) are recognized as employee  benefit expense as incurred. Remeasurements (including actuarial gains and losses and return on plan assets, net of interest) are recognized in other comprehensive income and included in retained earnings as incurred and are not reclassified to profit or loss in subsequent periods.

The  net defined benefit liability (asset) represents the deficit ("surplus") of contributions to a defined benefit retirement plan. The net defined benefit asset may not exceed the present value of the refund of contributions from the plan or the reduction of future contributions.

## (XX)  Income Taxes

Income tax expense is the sum of current income tax and deferred income tax.

## 1. Current Income Tax

The Group determines its income (loss) for the current period in accordance with the regulations  of  each  jurisdiction  in  which  it  files  income  tax  returns  and  calculates  the income tax payable (recoverable) accordingly.

Income tax on undistributed earnings calculated in accordance with the R.O.C. Income Tax Act is recognized in the year when the shareholders' meeting approves the resolution.

Adjustments to prior years' income tax payable are included in the current income tax.

## 2. Deferred income tax

Deferred income tax is calculated as the temporary difference between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities and the tax basis of taxable income.

Deferred  income  tax  liabilities  are  generally  recognized  for  all  taxable  temporary differences, while deferred income tax assets are recognized to the extent that it is probable that taxable income will be available against which deductible temporary differences can be utilized.

Deferred  income  tax  liabilities  are  recognized  for  taxable  temporary  differences related to investments in subsidiaries and associates, except where the Group can control the timing of the reversal of the temporary difference and it is probable that the temporary difference  will  not  reverse  in  the  foreseeable  future.  Deferred  income  tax  assets  are recognized for deductible temporary differences related to such investments only to the extent  that  it  is  probable  that  sufficient  taxable  income  will  be  available  to  allow  the temporary differences to be realized and the reversal is expected in the foreseeable future.

The carrying amount of deferred tax assets is reviewed at each balance sheet date and reduced to the extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable income will be available  to  allow  all  or  part  of  the  asset  to  be  recovered.  For  those  not  previously recognized as deferred income tax assets, the carrying amount is also reviewed at each balance sheet date and increased to the extent that it is probable that the taxable income will be available to recover all or part of the asset in the future.

Deferred  income  tax  assets  and  liabilities  are  measured  at  the  tax  rates  that  are expected to apply to the period when the liability is settled or the asset is realized, based on tax rates and tax laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the balance sheet date. Deferred income tax liabilities and assets are measured to reflect the tax consequences of the manner in which the Group expects to recover or settle the carrying amount of its assets and liabilities at the balance sheet date.

## 3. Current and Deferred Income Taxes

Current and deferred income taxes are recognized in profit or loss, except for current and deferred income taxes related to items recognized in other comprehensive income or directly in equity, which are recognized in other comprehensive income or directly in equity, respectively.

## V. Main Sources of Uncertainty in Significant Accounting Judgments, Estimates, and Assumptions

In  adopting  accounting  policies,  the  Group's  management  is  required  to  make  judgments, estimates  and  assumptions  based  on  historical  experience  and  other  relevant  factors  when  the information is not readily available from other sources. Actual results may differ from those estimates.

The Group considers the recent development of the COVID-19 pandemic and its possible impact on  the  economic  environment  as  part  of  its  significant  accounting  estimates  related  to  cash  flow projections,  growth  rates,  discount  rates,  profitability,  etc.  Management  reviews  estimates  and underlying assumptions on an ongoing basis. If a revision of an estimate affects only the current period, it is recognized in the period in which it is revised; if a revision of an accounting estimate affects both the current and future periods, it is recognized in the period in which it is revised and in the future period.

## Main sources of uncertainty in estimates and assumptions

## Inventory Impairment

The net realizable value of inventories is the estimated selling price under normal circumstances, less  the  estimated  selling  expenses  to  be  incurred.  These  estimates  are  based  on  current  market conditions  and  historical  sales  experience  of  similar  products.  Changes  in  market  conditions  may materially affect these estimates.

The expected credit losses over the period of continuation are calculated using an allowance matrix, which takes into account the customer's past default history and current financial condition, the economic situation of the industry, as well as the GDP forecast and industry outlook. As the Company's credit loss history shows that the loss patterns of different customer groups differ, the Company distinguishes customer groups based on credit ratings and calculates expected credit loss rates based on a provision matrix, taking into account historical experience, current market conditions and forward-looking information.

## (III) Major Lease Activities and Terms

The Group leases certain buildings for use as offices and retail stores for periods of 1 to 15 years. Some of the store leases provide for variable lease payments based on a specified percentage of the store's gross sales. At the end of the lease term, the Group does not have preferential acquisition rights on the leased buildings, and the Group is not allowed to sublease or assign all or part of the subject of the lease without the lessor's consent.

The Group leases a large amount of real estate to establish stores for its retail business. These lease terms are negotiated by the management of each business unit and include various lease payment terms. The Group included variable payments in the lease terms in order to reduce  the  fixed  costs  of  the  newly  established  stores  or  to  control  the  profitability  and flexibility of operations. The variable lease payment terms vary significantly within the Group.

4. The  majority  of  variable  payments  are  based  on  a  specified  percentage  of  store turnover.
5. Variable payments represent approximately 5% to 40% of the total lease payments for individual real estate; and
6. Certain variable payment provisions contain a floor clause.

The variable payment clause results in higher rental costs for stores with higher turnover, but the clause helps the Group's profit management.

The Group expects to change the rent expense as a percentage of store sales in the future to be the same as the current year.

From 2022, due to the severe impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the market economy, the Group negotiated with each lessor on the lease of the subject matter of the lease, and the lessor  agreed  to  reduce  the  rental  amount  based  on  the  results  of  the  negotiation,  and  the

amount of Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities was reduced by NT$6,905 thousand upon the occurrence of the reduction event or situation.

From 2021, due to the severe impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the market economy, the Group negotiated with each lessor on the lease of the subject matter of the lease, and the lessor  agreed  to  reduce  the  rental  amount  based  on  the  results  of  the  negotiation,  and  the amount of Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities was reduced by NT$12,947 thousand upon the occurrence of the reduction event or situation.

## Second issuance of domestic unsecured convertible corporate bonds

The Company issued 3 thousand units of unsecured convertible corporate bonds in Taiwan on March  2,  2020  at  an  interest  rate  of  0%  in  New  Taiwan  dollars  with  a  principal  amount  of NT$300,000 thousand.

- (1) Holders of each corporate bond unit shall be entitled to convert into ordinary shares of the Company at NT$65.3 per share. The conversion period is June 3, 2020 to March 2, 2025.
- (2) If the corporate bonds are not converted by then, the circulating corporate bonds will be called in cash at face value on March 2, 2025.
- (3) The day of 3 years from the issue date (March 2, 2023) shall be the basis date for the sellback of the bonds. The bonds may be sold back to the Company based on the face value of the bonds plus interest compensation, which is 100.75% of the face value of the bonds (0.25% real rate of return) after three years from the issue date (March 2, 2023)

The  convertible  corporate  bonds  consist  of  liabilities  and  equity  components,  which  are expressed  as  capital  reserves  -  stock  options  under  equity.  The  effective  interest  rate  originally recognized for the liability component is 1.66%.

The convertible corporate bonds consist of a liability component and an equity component. The equity component is recognized under equity as a capital surplus - stock option, and the effective interest  rate  on  the  liability  component  is  initially  recognized  at  1.66%.  The  face  value  of  the convertible bonds exercised in 2022 and 2021 was NT$71,000 thousand and NT$80,300 thousand, respectively,  which  were  converted  to  common  stock  of  NT$10,867  thousand  and  NT$10,910 thousand, respectively. In addition, as a result of the exercise of the conversion rights and redemption of bonds, the capital surplus - stock options of convertible bonds recognized in the original issue were reduced by NT$4,102 thousand and NT$4,639 thousand, the discount on bonds payable was reduced by NT$2,653 thousand and NT$4,580 thousand, and the net conversion amount exceeded the  face  value  of  the  converted  common  stock  was  transferred  to  capital  surplus  -  conversion premiums of convertible bonds of NT$64,152 thousand and NT$72,354 thousand, respectively.

## XXIV. Retirement benefit plan

## (I) Defined Contribution Plan

Among  the  Group,  the  Company,  PROTERANN  HEALTHCARE,  INC.,  SINEWY CHOICE PHARMACEUTICALS CO., LTD. and TAIWAN TRIM CO. LTD. are under the pension system of the Labor Pension Act. The pension system is a government-administered defined contribution pension plan that contributes 6% of employees' monthly salaries to the individual accounts of the Bureau of Labor Insurance.

## (II) Defined Benefit Plan

The Company's pension plan under the Labor Standards Act is a defined benefit pension plan administered by the government. Employees' pension payments are based on the years of service and the average salary for the six months before the approved retirement date. Under this system, these companies contribute 2% of employees' monthly salaries to the pension fund, which is deposited in the name of the Supervisory Committee of Business Entities' Labor Retirement Reserve to a dedicated account in the Bank of Taiwan. Before the end of the year, if the balance in the account is not sufficient to pay for the workers who are expected to meet the retirement requirements in the following year, the difference will be disbursed in one lump sum by the end of March of the following year. The Group does not have the right to influence

the investment management strategy as the account is entrusted to the Bureau of Labor Funds of the Ministry of Labor.

The Group is exposed to the following risks due to the Labor Standards Act's pension system:

1. Investment risk: The Bureau of Labor Funds, Ministry of Labor, invests the Labor Pension Fund in domestic (and foreign) equity securities, debt securities and bank deposits  through  its  own  operations  and  entrusted  management.  However,  the amount allocated to the Group's plan assets is based on a return no less than the interest rate of a two-year time deposit with a local bank.
2. Interest rate risk: A decrease in interest rates on government bonds will increase the present value of the defined benefit obligation, which will be partially offset by an increase in the return on debt investments in plan assets.
3. Salary  risk:  The  present  value  of  the  defined  benefit  obligation  is  calculated  by reference to the future salaries of the plan members. Therefore, an increase in plan members' salaries will increase the present value of the defined benefit obligation.

The present value of the Group's defined benefit obligation was actuarially determined by a qualified actuary and the significant assumptions at the measurement date were as follows:

| December 31, 2022  December 31, 2021  Discount rate  1.25%  0.60%  Expected rate of salary increase  2.00%  1.50%   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| December 31, 2022  December 31, 2021  Discount rate  Increase of 0.25%  ( $  471 )  ( $  519 )  Decrease of 0.25%  $  487  $  540  Expected rate of salary increase  Increase of 1%  $  2,024  $  2,250  Decrease of 1%  ( $  1,792 )  ( $  1,963 )   |

## (III) Retained earnings and dividend policy

In accordance with the reserve allocation policy of the Company, if there is the reserve in the annual accounts, it should firstly make up the accumulated deficit, draw 10% for the legal  reserve,  and  designate  or  return  the  special  reserve  in  accordance  with  the  rules  or competent  authority  provisions;  if  there  is  still  reserve  and  the  accumulated  undistributed reserve, the Board of Directors shall draw up a proposal for the distribution of the reserve and submit  to  the  shareholders'  meeting  for  a  resolution  to  distribute  the  dividend  to  the shareholders. Refer to Note XXVII (VIII) employee remuneration and director &amp; supervisor remuneration  for  the  employee  and  director  remuneration  allocation  policy  of Articles  of Incorporation.

In  addition,  on  the  basis  of  the  Company's Articles  of  Incorporation,  the  Company's dividend policy coordinates with the current and future development plans, in consideration of  the  investment  environment,  financial  planning  and  competition  situation  at  home  and abroad,  and  the  shareholder  dividend  is  distributed  in  principle  of  more  than  30%  of  the distributable reserve; when distributing the dividend, it shall be in the way of cash or stock, in which the cash dividend shall not be less than 10% of the total dividend.

At the general shareholders' meeting held on May 26, 2022 and August 23, 2021, the Company  resolved  to  approve  the  following  earnings  distribution  for  2021  and  2020, respectively.

## XXXIII.  Capital Risk Management

The  Group  undertakes  capital  management  to  ensure  that  the  Group's  businesses  are  able  to maximize shareholder returns by optimizing debt and equity balances while continuing to operate. There is no change in the overall strategy of the Group.

The capital structure of the Group consists of the Group's net liability (i.e., loans less cash and cash equivalents) and equity attributable to the owners of the Company (i.e., equity, capital reserve, retained earnings and other equity items).

The Group is not subject to other external capital requirements.

The Group's key management reviews the Group's capital structure on a quarterly basis, which includes consideration of the cost of various types of capital and the related risks. The Group will balance its overall capital structure by paying dividends, issuing new shares, buying back shares, and issuing new debt or paying off old debt, as recommended by key management.

## (IV)  Financial Risk Management Objectives and Policies

The  Group's  major  financial  instruments  include  investments  in  equity  and  debt instruments, accounts receivable, accounts payable, corporate bonds payable, loans and lease liabilities. The Group's financial management department provides services to each business unit, coordinates access to domestic and international financial markets, and monitors and manages  the  financial  risks  associated  with  the  Group's  operations  through  internal  risk reporting that analyzes risk exposures based on the level and breadth of risk. These risks include  market  risk  (including  exchange  rate  risk  and  interest  rate  risk),  credit  risk  and liquidity risk.

1. Market Risk
- (3) Exchange rate risk

Several subsidiaries of the Group have bank deposits denominated in nonfunctional currencies, which expose the Group to exchange rate fluctuations.

The  Company's  carrying  amounts  of  monetary  assets  and  liabilities denominated in non-functional currencies as of the balance sheet date are shown in Note XXXVIII.

## Sensitivity Analysis

The Company is primarily affected by fluctuations in the exchange rate of the Taiwan dollar against the U.S. dollar.

When the exchange rate of the New Taiwan dollar (functional currency) increases and decreases by 1% against the U.S. dollar, 1% is the sensitivity ratio used  for  internal  reporting  of  exchange  rate  risk  to  key  management  and represents management's assessment of the reasonably possible range of changes in  foreign  currency  exchange  rates. The  sensitivity  analysis  includes  only foreign  currency  monetary  items  in  circulation  and  adjusts  their  year-end translation by a 1% change in the exchange rate. A 1% weakening of the New Taiwan dollar against the U.S. dollar would increase the Company's net income before income taxes by NT$997 thousand and NT$691 thousand in 2022 and 2021, respectively.

This  was  mainly  due  to  the  Company's  U.S.  dollar-denominated  time

deposits and accounts payable that were outstanding and not cash flow hedged as of the balance sheet date.

The Company's sensitivity to foreign exchange rates increased during the year due to the increase in U.S. dollar-denominated time deposits, resulting in an increase in the balance of U.S. dollar-denominated time deposits.

## (4) Interest Rate Risk

The Group's interest rate risk arises mainly from fixed- and floating-rate time deposits, loans, lease liabilities and corporate bonds payable, resulting in the interest rate risk.

The carrying amounts of the Group's financial assets and financial liabilities exposed to the interest rate risk as of the balance sheet date were as follows:

| December 31, 2022  December 31, 2021  With  fair  value  interest  rate risk  －  Financial asset  $  289,921  $  264,752  －  Financial liability  2,673,178  2,254,150  With  cash  flow  interest  rate risk  －  Financial asset  865,831  768,234  －  Financial liability  1,262,000  1,355,500   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## Sensitivity Analysis

The sensitivity analysis below is based on the interest rate risk of derivative and  non-derivative  instruments  at  the  balance  sheet  date.  For  floating  rate liabilities, the analysis assumes that the amount of the liability outstanding at the balance  sheet  date  is  outstanding  at  the  whole  reporting  period.  The  rate  of change used in reporting interest rates internally to key management is a 1% increase  or  decrease  in  interest  rates,  which  also  represents  management's assessment of the reasonably possible range of interest rate changes.

If the interest rate increases or decreases by 1%, with all other variables held constant, the Group's before-tax net income would decrease by $3,962 thousand and $5,873 thousand in 2022 and 2021, respectively, mainly due to the risk of the Group's variable-rate loans.

The Group's sensitivity to interest rates decreased during the year, mainly due to the decrease in variable-rate debt instruments.

## 2. Credit Risk

Credit risk refers to the risk of financial loss caused by the counter-parties' default on  contractual  obligations.  The  Group's  counter-parties  are  mostly  contractors  of shopping malls for a certain period of time, and the Group continuously monitors the accounts receivable balance, so the risk of bad debts is not significant.

The Group's customer base is large and unrelated, so the concentration of credit risk is not high.

The  credit  risk  is  limited  because  the  counter-parties  of  liquidity  are  banks supervised by the People's Republic of China and the Republic of China.

## 3. Liquidity risk

The  Group  manages  and  maintains  a  sufficient  portion  of  cash  and  cash equivalents to support the Group's operations and mitigate the impact of cash flow fluctuations. The management of the Group monitors the use of banking facilities and ensures compliance with the terms of borrowing contracts.

Bank loans are an important source of liquidity for the Group. As of December 31, 2022, the Group still has a line of credit of NT$979,000 thousand available for

back-up and there is no doubt about its liquidity and financial structure. The Group's unutilized facilities are described in (2) Financing Facilities below.

Segment  profit  is  defined  as  the  profit  earned  by  each  segment,  excluding  share  of headquarter management costs and director remuneration, loss on disposal of financial assets, finance  costs,  impairment  loss  on  goodwill,  interest  income,  gain  or  loss  on  disposal  of property, plant and equipment, gain or loss on disposal of non-current assets held for sale, net foreign currency translation gain, gain or loss on valuation of financial instruments, gain or loss on lease modification, and other non-operating gains or losses. This measure is provided to the chief operating decision maker for the purpose of allocating resources to the segment and evaluating its performance.

Goodwill is allocated to reportable segments. Assets used jointly by reportable segments are allocated on the basis of the revenue earned by each reportable segment.
